lanes.summary: MT-01 (NFR-08 observability) is verified for real against the wave-3 tree and is substantially PASS: registration, listing create/update/cancel, booking create/cancel/complete/promote and media attach/delete each emit exactly one structured JSON audit record carrying event, correlation ID, actor user ID, subject entity ID, outcome and ISO timestamp; the request's correlation ID is stamped on every outbox row the same transaction wrote and reappears verbatim on the worker's delivered/retry/dead-letter lines (both sides asserted); error records carry message, stack, correlation ID and HTTP status while the response body stays generic; and two independent captured log corpora contain user IDs only — no email, password, name, phone, street address or postal code, with a generic email-shaped regex sweep returning zero hits. MT-01's fourth named action, a MODERATION DECISION, is not performable: I probed four plausible surfaces and all 404, so that action (and SRS §4.6's "records needed to audit IT-03 moderation decisions") is reported not_implemented, not skipped. UT-01 / NFR-07 is not_implemented end to end — client/ does not exist, no .jsx/.tsx file exists anywhere in the repo, no axe-core or headless-browser dependency is installed, and the declared `npm run test:a11y` script additionally fails in this environment on a ChromeDriver/Chrome version mismatch; the 5-participant moderated study is a human activity and is marked untestable. One genuine wave-3 defect reproduced (the previously suspected ADRC-W3-01/W3-F2): the listing audit records serialise the MEHKO local date as a stringified JS Date ("Mon Aug 17 2026 00:00:00 GMT-0700 (Pacific Daylight Time)") instead of the "2026-08-17" the wire serializer emits — three new failing assertions pin it. The previously-listed MTUT-02 order-sensitive identity test is RESOLVED: tests/unit/identity.test.js passes both standalone (40/40, 10.9 s) and in full-suite order. Lane files added: tests/mt-ut-quality/mt01-wave3-audit-gaps.test.js (12 tests, 9 pass / 3 fail-by-design); the two pre-existing lane files pass 22/22. Non-lane observation for the report author: under concurrent verifier load on this host, tests/rt-lt-resilience/lt01-lt02-wave3.test.js (200-VU p95 gate) and tests/unit/db.test.js (volume seed, "Connection terminated unexpectedly") failed in one run and passed in the next — those are machine-contention flakes from parallel lanes, not reproducible defects, and I am not claiming them. All lane files pass eslint and prettier; `npm run build` reports 83 files parse cleanly and createApp() boots.

findings.title: Listing audit records log the MEHKO local date as a stringified JS Date, not the YYYY-MM-DD LA calendar day (AB-03 / NFR-08)
findings.failureScenario: POST /api/listings with scheduledStart = now()+72h and X-Correlation-Id: mt01gap-create-<run> returns 201 whose body carries listing.localDate = "2026-08-17" (correct, produced by serializers.isoCalendarDate). The audit line emitted for the same request carries localDate = "Mon Aug 17 2026 00:00:00 GMT-0700 (Pacific Daylight Time)". Identical defect on PATCH /api/listings/:id ("Tue Aug 18 2026 00:00:00 GMT-0700 (Pacific Daylight Time)") and POST /api/listings/:id/cancel ("Mon Aug 24 2026 00:00:00 GMT-0700 (Pacific Daylight Time)"). Cause: src/modules/listings/service.js:169, :384 and :441 do `localDate: String(row.local_date)`, and node-postgres parses a DATE column into a JS Date at PROCESS-LOCAL midnight, so Date.prototype.toString() stamps the deploy host's offset onto the record. Verified with `TZ=Europe/Paris node -e "SELECT DATE '2026-08-17'"` → 'Mon Aug 17 2026 00:00:00 GMT+0200 (Central European Summer Time)' and TZ=Asia/Tokyo → '...GMT+0900 (Japan Standard Time)'. Consequences: (a) AB-03's acceptance — listing creations reviewable by host ID and local date — cannot be satisfied by a log query, because the field is not a comparable/sortable calendar day and does not match the format the API, the DB column and mehko.localDateFor all use; (b) on any non-LA deploy host the record advertises a timezone label (e.g. 'Japan Standard Time') that contradicts ADR-009's mandate that MEHKO day boundaries are evaluated in America/Los_Angeles, actively misleading anyone auditing a one-listing-per-host-per-day dispute; (c) the audit record disagrees with the wire response for the same entity in the same request. Reproduce: `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://homeplate:homeplate@localhost:5432/homeplate_mtut_test TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/7 OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET=homeplate-media-mtut-test npx jest tests/mt-ut-quality/mt01-wave3-audit-gaps.test.js --runInBand` → 3 failed, 9 passed.
findings.proposedFix: Reuse the projection that already exists for exactly this hazard instead of adding a second one. In src/modules/listings/serializers.js add `isoCalendarDate` to module.exports (line 188-195; the function itself at line ~100 is already correct and deliberately reads the Date's LOCAL components so it recovers the SQL calendar date on any server timezone). Then in src/modules/listings/service.js replace `localDate: String(row.local_date)` at line 169 (listing.created), line 384 (listing.updated) and `localDate: String(result.row.local_date)` at line 441 (listing.cancelled) with `localDate: serializers.isoCalendarDate(...)` — `serializers` is already required in that file. Equivalent alternative if you prefer to fix it at the source: have src/modules/listings/repo.js select `local_date::text AS local_date` so pg never hands the layer a Date at all; isoCalendarDate already passes strings through unchanged, so the serializer keeps working either way. Do NOT use mehko.localDateFor(row.local_date) here — re-projecting a process-local-midnight instant into LA reintroduces an off-by-one on non-LA hosts (the serializer's own comment says so). After the change the three assertions in tests/mt-ut-quality/mt01-wave3-audit-gaps.test.js block A pass with no test edit; the sibling assertion in tests/mt-ut-quality/mt01-wave3-booking-audit.test.js:168 (`typeof rec.localDate === 'string'`) is unaffected.

findings.title: Worker-initiated booking.promoted audit record omits the actor entirely (MT-01 requires an actor on every record)
findings.failureScenario: Create a booking with X-Correlation-Id: mt01gap-promote-<run>, make the promotion due (`UPDATE listings SET scheduled_start = now()`, `UPDATE outbox_jobs SET available_at = now() - interval '1 minute' WHERE type='booking.promote'`) and drain the real worker with pollOnce. The booking transitions to in_progress and exactly one audit record is emitted, correctly carrying correlationId = the originating request's ID. Its full key set, captured by a probe run of tests/mt-ut-quality/mt01-wave3-audit-gaps.test.js, is ["level","time","service","correlationId","jobId","jobType","attempt","audit","event","outcome","entityType","entityId","msg"] — there is no actorUserId key at all. MT-01's acceptance requires event name, correlation/request ID, ACTOR USER ID, subject entity ID, outcome and timestamp on each record. A reviewer filtering audit lines by actor therefore silently loses every system-driven lifecycle transition, and cannot distinguish 'promoted by the scheduler' from 'field dropped by a bug'. Every user-driven site in src/modules/bookings/service.js (lines 90, 179, 258, 333) does pass actorUserId, so the omission is specific to the worker path.
findings.proposedFix: In src/modules/bookings/lifecycle.js:254, make the system actor explicit rather than absent: `audit(log, { event: 'booking.promoted', outcome: 'success', actorUserId: null, actor: 'system:outbox', entityType: 'booking', entityId: bookingId })`. `actor` is not a PII-register key and is not caught by the logger's redaction suffix list, so it passes through intact. If the team prefers a single shape for all system events, add the same pair to any future worker-emitted audit call and note the convention in the src/lib/logger.js audit() contract comment (lines 14-16) so wave-4 handlers follow it. No test change is required; tests/mt-ut-quality/mt01-wave3-audit-gaps.test.js documents the observed shape in a comment at the promote test and can then be tightened to assert `actor === 'system:outbox'`.

findings.title: The declared UT-01 accessibility toolchain (`npm run test:a11y`) cannot run and would not cover NFR-07's key interfaces
findings.failureScenario: `npm run test:a11y` on this machine prints 'Running axe-core 4.13.0 in chrome-headless' then 'Error: session not created: This version of ChromeDriver only supports Chrome version 152 / Current browser version is 151.0.7922.138 with binary path /Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome' and exits without auditing anything. Three separate problems compound: (1) the script resolves @axe-core/cli through `npx --yes` at run time rather than a pinned devDependency, so the ChromeDriver it fetches is unpinned against whatever Chrome the developer has — the run is not reproducible and cannot be put in CI as written; (2) it targets exactly one URL, http://localhost:5173, while NFR-07's acceptance in requirements-inventory.json enumerates seven interfaces (search/browse, listing detail, host profile, booking flow, signup/login, messaging, moderator queue) that each need their own audit at wcag2a/wcag2aa with zero serious/critical violations; (3) nothing starts a server on 5173 — `curl -m 5 http://localhost:5173` returns HTTP 000 (curl exit 7) — and client/ does not exist, so the script has never had a subject. This is why UT-01 is reported not_implemented rather than failing: the check has no runnable harness behind it.
findings.proposedFix: Treat this as a wave-5 deliverable rather than an existing capability. When client/ lands: add `@axe-core/playwright` (or `@axe-core/puppeteer`) plus the browser package as pinned devDependencies so the browser is vendored and version-locked instead of resolved by `npx --yes`; replace the single-URL script with a Jest/Playwright spec under tests/mt-ut-quality/ that boots the Vite preview server, visits each of the seven routes from NFR-07's acceptance list, runs axe with `withTags(['wcag2a','wcag2aa'])`, and fails on any violation of impact 'serious' or 'critical'; add the keyboard-traversal spot checks (Tab order reaches every interactive control, focus indicator visible, form controls labelled, errors announced via aria-live) as assertions in the same spec. Until then, keep the `test:a11y` script but make its failure honest — either point it at a `--chromedriver-path` the repo controls or drop it from package.json so no one reads its presence as coverage. The 5-participant moderated study (SRS §4.5) stays a scheduled human activity and must be recorded with participants, date and triage outcome before NFR-07 can be closed.

lanes.summary: Independently re-verified TC-01..TC-07 (FR-01..FR-07) against the working tree (commit 3136b91 + verifier test files). The four wave-3 acceptance suites already on disk pass, and I added tests/tc-core/tc01-04-acceptance-gaps.test.js (8 new tests) covering the acceptance clauses they did not exercise: the ADR-005 geocode-coordinate cache TTL, the {page,pageSize,total} paging contract, the ADR-009 localDate wire format, unapproved-review invisibility on the FR-02 read path, NFR-12 deleted-media/deleted-account handling on FR-03, and concurrent dual confirmation plus per-booking participant identity on FR-04. Lane result: 6 suites / 62 tests pass (1.4 s). FR-01..FR-04 PASS. FR-05/FR-06/FR-07 are NOT IMPLEMENTED — src/modules/{reviews,messaging,moderation,safety} are absent and the endpoints answer a structured JSON 404, proven by execution; only their §3.4 schema substrate exists. Re-derived the named wave-3 residuals in my scope: ADRC-W3-01 (localDate serialized as a timezone-dependent instant) is FIXED — GET /api/listings/:id returns "2033-06-14" for a listing stored on LA day 2033-06-14 with UTC day 2033-06-15. Full committed suite measured green at 46 suites / 945 tests, npm run lint clean, npm run build clean. Five reproducible minor findings, no blockers and no major defects in this lane.

findings.title: FR-02 detail returns host:null instead of a host summary when the host is soft-deleted or has no host_profiles row
findings.failureScenario: Reproduced twice by probe against the live app (tests/tc-core/zz-probe.test.js, run then removed). (a) Seed host + host_profile + approved listing, then UPDATE users SET deleted_at = now() WHERE id = <host>. GET /api/listings/<listing> as an authenticated viewer → 200 with listing.host === null (logged: 'PROBE detail status 200 host= null'). (b) Seed a host with can_publish_listing but NO host_profiles row plus an approved listing → GET /api/listings/<listing> → 200 with listing.host === null. The FR-02 acceptance requires 'host summary (display name, bio, average rating, review count)' in the same response; the caller instead gets a null with no displayName even though users.full_name exists and the reviews array is still populated. hostContextFor (src/modules/listings/service.js) hands back host:null whenever hostsRepo.findHost returns null, and findHost requires BOTH a host_profiles join AND users.deleted_at IS NULL. Neither trigger is reachable through the v1.0 API today (there is no account-deletion endpoint until wave-4 U4-PRIVACY, and requireEligibility(PUBLISH_LISTING) demands host_profile_complete), so this is a latent defect that bites the moment wave-4 deletion ships — which is why it is reported rather than deferred.
findings.proposedFix: In hostContextFor, fall back to a users-only summary (displayName from users.full_name or hostSerializers.ANONYMIZED_AUTHOR, bio null) plus the review aggregates instead of returning null, so the FR-02 contract holds for every listing that is itself visible; alternatively make the wave-4 erasure path cancel/hide the deleted host's listings so the null case cannot be reached (see TCC-02, which shares the trigger).

findings.title: A soft-deleted host's approved listings stay fully discoverable in FR-01 search and FR-02 detail
findings.failureScenario: Reproduced by probe: seed host + approved/active/future listing with cuisine probecuisine<RUN>, then UPDATE users SET deleted_at = now() WHERE id = <host>. GET /api/listings/search?cuisine=probecuisine<RUN> still returns 200 with 1 result (logged: 'PROBE search status 200 n= 1'), and GET /api/listings/<id> still returns 200. Neither search.repo.searchListings nor listings.repo.findById joins users to exclude deleted_at accounts, even though hosts.repo.findHost does — so the same host is simultaneously 404 on GET /api/hosts/:id and fully browsable/bookable through their listings. This is the NFR-12 erasure direction and it is the trigger that makes TCC-01 visible. Wave-4 U4-PRIVACY owns the deletion cascade, so this is flagged now so the cascade is specified to cover listings, not left to be discovered later.
findings.proposedFix: Decide the erasure cascade explicitly in U4-PRIVACY: on account deletion, cancel (or hide) the host's active listings in the same transaction, and/or add AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM users u WHERE u.id = l.host_id AND u.deleted_at IS NULL) to the search and detail visibility predicates so the source of truth alone cannot expose a deleted host's meals.

findings.title: FR-01 acceptance clause unmet: a page-cache-served query during a Maps outage carries no degraded-mode flag
findings.failureScenario: Reproduced by probe against the live app: warm the page cache with GET /api/listings/search?location=<loc>&cuisine=<c> (200, 1 result), then jest.spyOn(maps,'searchArea').mockRejectedValue(new Error('outage')) and repeat the identical query. Observed: status 200, results length 1, adapter call count 0, and body.degraded === undefined (logged: 'PROBE during outage status 200 degraded= undefined n= 1 adapterCalls= 0'). The FR-01 acceptance in requirements-inventory.json states 'With the Maps adapter forced to fail, a previously cached query still returns results plus a degraded-mode flag (NFR-09)' — the results half holds, the flag half does not. Note the conflict direction: SRS §2.5 only requires degraded mode to 'serve cached or previously stored data where available' and says nothing about flagging a page-cache hit, and src/modules/search/service.js:160-188 deliberately flags only the adapter's own stale-copy answer, so this may be an over-strict acceptance sentence rather than a code defect. Reporting it rather than silently choosing a side.
findings.proposedFix: Pick one and record it: either (a) have searchListings detect that the page cache answered while the provider is unreachable and set degraded:true on that response too, or (b) correct the FR-01 acceptance sentence in docs/_generated/requirements-inventory.json to say the degraded flag accompanies a STALE-CACHE ADAPTER answer, while a fresh page-cache hit is a normal 200 (which is what src/modules/search/service.js documents in its own header). Do not silently leave the two disagreeing.

findings.title: FR-02 detail truncates the host's approved reviews to 5 with no total or cursor on the reviews array
findings.failureScenario: Reproduced by probe: seed a host with 7 approved reviews, then GET /api/listings/<listing> → listing.reviews.length === 5 while listing.host.reviewCount === 7 (logged: 'PROBE reviews returned 5 reviewCount 7'). hostContextFor passes PROFILE_REVIEWS_LIMIT = 5 (src/modules/hosts/service.js:33) with no offset and the payload carries no reviewsTotal, nextPage or link, so the FR-02 clause 'and the approved reviews for that host' is satisfied only partially and a client cannot tell from the reviews array alone that it is truncated. Mitigating: host.reviewCount discloses the true total and GET /api/hosts/:id/reviews?page=N pages the remainder, so no data is unreachable.
findings.proposedFix: Either add an explicit disclosure to the detail payload (e.g. reviews plus reviewsTotal/reviewsPageSize, or a documented pointer to GET /api/hosts/:id/reviews) or state the 5-item preview explicitly in the FR-02 acceptance so the truncation is specified rather than incidental.

findings.title: tc01-search's Redis page-cache assertion is contention-sensitive and can fail spuriously under machine load
findings.failureScenario: Observed once in three full-suite runs on this machine while other verifier lanes were running concurrently (four processes hitting the same PostgreSQL/Redis/MinIO): tests/tc-core/tc01-search.test.js:215 failed with 'expect(pageKeys.length).toBeGreaterThan(0) — Expected: > 0, Received: 0' after scanning hp:cache:search:page:*. The same file passes in isolation and passed in the two subsequent full runs (46 suites / 945 tests green). Root cause is by design, not a product bug: src/lib/cache.set swallows Redis errors so a contended/timed-out cache write is silently dropped ('a failed cache write costs latency, never correctness'), which makes any test that asserts a cache key EXISTS non-deterministic under load. Three other tracked suites (tests/unit/adapter-maps.test.js, tests/tc-booking/tc13-notifications.test.js, tests/unit/hosts-media.test.js) failed in the same contended run and passed when re-run alone, so the sensitivity is not unique to this lane.
findings.proposedFix: Make the assertion resilient without weakening it: after the search, poll the hp:cache:search:page:* scan for up to ~1 s before asserting, or assert the cache effect behaviourally (second identical query performs zero adapter calls — already asserted in the same test) and downgrade the raw key-existence scan to a check that runs only when at least one key is present. Also record in docs/verification-report.md that lanes run in parallel must use per-lane TEST_DATABASE_URL/TEST_REDIS_URL/OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET AND that latency/cache-existence assertions are only authoritative on an otherwise idle machine.

lanes.summary: Executed RT-01, RT-02, LT-01 and LT-02 against commit 3136b91 on live infra (PostgreSQL 16 / Redis 7 / MinIO via docker compose). Final lane state: 9 suites / 52 tests passing on isolated resources. Authoritative LT-01 measurement (200 VUs, 5 min, against the NFR-02 volume dataset of 10,000 users / 1,000 listings / 1,000 bookings / 1,001 approved reviews): 791,709 requests, 0 errors, overall p95 = 253.7 ms, per-endpoint p95 search 5.7 / hostReviews 179.4 / listingDetail 297.7 / hostPage 354.6 ms — the NFR-01 500 ms budget is met with margin, measured while six sibling verifier lanes loaded the machine (load avg ~24-30 on 12 cores), so the numbers are pessimistic. All RT-01 outage drills pass including the ADR-002 property that a moderation outage leaves public content PENDING, and all RT-02 crash/idempotency/backoff/dead-letter properties pass. Two residuals I was told to check hardest are RESOLVED on the current tree and I proved it with new tests: IT3-F1 (booking.promote self-dedupe) is fixed in src/modules/bookings/lifecycle.js securePromotionSchedule and now has a direct regression test; F-1 (standalone lane scripts bypassing the suite advisory lock) is fixed — lt01-run.js is the only CLI entry under tests/ and it acquires the lock. The one significant defect I found is in the verification harness, not the product: nothing prevents two concurrent lanes from picking the same Redis DB index, and when that happened a sibling lane's FLUSHDB wiped my sessions mid-run and produced a completely false NFR-01 failure (99.05% error rate, all 401). I reproduced that with redis-cli MONITOR and then re-measured on an exclusive index. NFR-01/NFR-02 latency checks are marked "partial" rather than "pass" for one honest reason only: k6 is not installed on this host, so the acceptance's literal k6 scenario was not the tool used; the substitute drives the real Express app over real loopback TCP at 200 concurrent connections.

checks.subject: NFR-09 / RT-01 drill 1 — Google Maps outage (ADR-005)
checks.evidence: npx jest tests/rt-lt-resilience/rt01-wave3-degradation.test.js --verbose → 6/6 drill-1 tests pass. Observed: healthy location search 200 and page cached; provider down + identical query served from cached page with ZERO adapter calls; provider down + stale area cache → 200 with degraded:true and the degraded page deliberately NOT cached; provider down + nothing cached → typed 503 SEARCH_DEGRADED, never a 500; non-location searches unaffected; recovery → 200 un-degraded. The user-facing message is real text, verified in src/modules/search/service.js:114 — 'Location search is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly, or search without a location.' Adapter-level equivalent also passes in rt01-degradation.test.js (live lookup → Redis cache → stale-with-indicator → typed 503 MAPS_UNAVAILABLE → recovery).

checks.subject: NFR-09 / FR-13 / RT-01 drill 2 — notification provider outage against POST /api/bookings
checks.evidence: Same run, drill 2 passes (1278 ms). Observed with mockTransport.injectFailures(1000): POST /api/bookings → 201 in <500 ms, booking row committed status 'pending'; exactly 2 notify.booking outbox rows committed with it, recipients = {guest, host}; one worker cycle → retried=2, deadLettered=0, both rows still 'pending' with attempt_count=1 and notification_attempts rows status='failed', mockTransport.deliveries() empty. After recovery the SAME deferred jobs deliver: delivered=2, exactly one delivery per recipient. The business write is untouched by the outage (FR-13 'provider failure shall not roll back or delay the booking transaction').

checks.subject: NFR-09 / ADR-002 / RT-01 drill 3 — moderation LLM outage leaves public content PENDING
checks.evidence: Same run, drill 3 passes (30 ms): with the LLM mock in outage mode, POST /api/listings still returns 201, the listing row's moderation_status stays 'pending', the listing is invisible to search, and the moderation work defers to the outbox — it never publishes unreviewed. Reinforced at the schema level by rt01-degradation.test.js 'public content stays PENDING by schema default — an outage cannot publish unreviewed content (ADR-002)'. This is the specific ADR-002 property the mandate calls out and it holds.

checks.subject: NFR-09 / ADR-004 / RT-01 drill 4 — object storage outage against GET /api/listings/:id
checks.evidence: Drill 4 passes (20 ms) with all three objectStorage operations (put/get/deleteByKey) patched to throw ServiceUnavailableError: GET /api/listings/:id returns 200 with one image whose URL is derived locally and contains the storage key — never a 500. I strengthened this drill because it was previously unfalsifiable: the read path derives URLs by pure local SigV4 arithmetic (src/lib/mediaUrls) and never calls the adapter at all, so the outage is structurally invisible. Added `expect(adapterCalls).toBe(0)`, which turns it into a real regression guard against anyone later putting a storage call on the read path. Re-ran: still 10/10 pass.

checks.subject: NFR-09 / RT-01 drill 5 — combined Google-side outage (Maps AND moderation LLM down together)
checks.evidence: Drill 5 passes (47 ms). With maps.searchArea and maps.geocode both throwing and llmMock.setOutage(true): POST /api/bookings → 201 (bookings still committable), POST /api/listings → 201 with moderation_status='pending' (public content stays pending), and non-location search still serves. This is the exact compound scenario named in the NFR-09 acceptance text. Adapter-level equivalent also passes in rt01-degradation.test.js drill 5.

checks.subject: NFR-09 — per-adapter resilience policy: 3000 ms timeout, bounded retries, exponential backoff
checks.evidence: Executed: config.adapters.timeoutMs === 3000 and resilience.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS === 3000; retryMax is a bounded integer >= 1; computeBackoffDelay(1/2/3) returns base, base*2, base*4 — genuinely exponential, not linear. Enforcement (not just configuration) is demonstrated behaviourally: rt01-degradation.test.js 'a hung provider is bounded by the per-attempt timeout, not hung forever' completes in 209 ms against an adapter that never settles, and rt01-notification-contract.test.js shows a total outage spending exactly config.adapters.retryMax+1 tries and stopping.

checks.subject: NFR-09 / ADR-011 — SendGrid and FCM adapters drilled as themselves
checks.evidence: Cannot be executed, by design, and I confirmed the mechanism rather than assuming it. src/config/schema.js:216 rejects config with 'NOTIFICATIONS_TRANSPORT must be mock when NODE_ENV=test (ADR-011)', so the suite can never resolve sendgrid.adapter or fcm.adapter; resolveAdapter() is also not exported, so it cannot be called with a synthetic cfg. This is the ADR-011 invariant working as intended (tests assert on persisted NOTIFICATION_ATTEMPT rows, never on a third party). What IS verifiable I did verify: both live adapters are driven through the single withResilience call in src/modules/notifications/transport.js:235 with config.adapters.timeoutMs / retryMax / backoffBaseMs, and that shared contract is exercised via the mock. No pass claimed for the live adapters themselves.

checks.subject: ADR-011 / NFR-09 — push gate defaults FALSE; provider outage yields a failed ROW, never a throw
checks.evidence: New file, 4/4 pass. Observed: config.notifications.push.enabled === false and config.notifications.transport === 'mock'; a push send returns {status:'failed', reason:'push_disabled'} with a notification_attempts row channel='push', status='failed', last_error matching /push channel refused/, and mockTransport.deliveries() empty — refused before any adapter ran. A total email outage (retryMax+6 injected failures) does NOT throw: it resolves {status:'failed'} with row.attempt_count === retryMax+1 exactly, sent_at NULL, zero deliveries. Recovery then yields status='sent' with sent_at set and exactly one delivery.

checks.subject: RT-02 — crash recovery: claim released, job re-claimed, delivered exactly once
checks.evidence: 2/2 pass. Observed: the claim really is FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED held inside an open transaction (asserted against src/outbox/worker.js CLAIM_SQL behaviour, not just its text); terminating the backend mid-processing rolls the claim back, the row stays 'pending', and redelivery happens exactly once (113-131 ms).

checks.subject: RT-02 — duplicate-delivery idempotency through the real handler
checks.evidence: Passes at both levels. Generic: a duplicate enqueue on the same dedupe_key is a no-op and redelivery after a lost commit does not double-send. Wave-3 notify.booking: a redelivered job completes again but the send happens exactly once (idempotencyKey reuses the existing notification_attempts row rather than sending). Backed by the ON CONFLICT (dedupe_key) DO NOTHING path in src/outbox/outbox.js returning {deduped:true} with the pre-existing row.

checks.subject: RT-02 — retry with exponential backoff, dead-letter, requeue
checks.evidence: Passes. A failing job backs off exponentially, dead-letters at config.outbox.maxAttempts with its failure reason retained in last_error, and requeueDeadLetter re-opens it with a fresh budget. Wave-3 equivalent for notify.booking passes in 4363 ms (real backoff waits observed, not mocked timers).

checks.subject: RT-02 — two concurrent workers never double-process a job
checks.evidence: Passes (381-394 ms): 6 jobs, 2 workers polling concurrently, every job handled exactly once. This is the SKIP LOCKED guarantee under real concurrency, not a simulation.

checks.subject: RT-02 — wave-3 handlers: notify.booking, booking.promote, listing.geocode
checks.evidence: 6/6 pass. notify.booking: exactly-once redelivery + dead-letter-with-reason + requeue. booking.promote: available_at equals the listing's scheduled_start, promotes when due, duplicate delivery no-ops, cancelled booking never promoted, start moved later re-enqueues for the new instant. listing.geocode: a Maps outage defers with backoff and recovery completes the SAME job writing both precisions, while a definitive no-results answer completes without retrying (retry cannot help).

checks.subject: RT-02 / IT3-F1 residual — booking.promote re-enqueue dedupe with an UNCHANGED scheduled_start
checks.evidence: RESOLVED on the current tree — verified, not assumed. The fix is src/modules/bookings/lifecycle.js securePromotionSchedule (lines 151-170): a deduped-onto row only counts as the surviving schedule when it is neither the row being delivered (deliveringJobId) nor a spent/claimed row, otherwise the key is disambiguated with the delivering row's id; if nothing can be secured it throws BOOKING_PROMOTE_UNSECURED so the worker keeps the row pending. I wrote a direct regression test for the exact dangerous case the existing suite did not cover (the existing test only moved the start, which changes the dedupe key and cannot reproduce it). New test forces the row due while leaving scheduled_start untouched, then asserts: pollOnce claimed=1 delivered=1, booking still 'pending' (not promoted early), exactly ONE live pending promote row that is NOT the delivered row and is scheduled for the same instant, and that this surviving row really does promote to 'in_progress' when the meal starts. A second test runs three successive early deliveries and asserts the 'exactly one live pending row' invariant holds after every cycle with zero dead-letters. 2/2 pass.

findings.title: Concurrent verifier lanes silently share a Redis DB index — a sibling lane's FLUSHDB wiped live sessions mid-run and produced a false NFR-01 failure (99.05% error rate)
findings.failureScenario: Reproduced end to end. tests/helpers/env.js documents a CONCURRENCY RULE promising that per-lane TEST_DATABASE_URL + TEST_REDIS_URL + OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET overrides give 'fully isolated resources (no lock needed)', but nothing verifies the Redis index or bucket is actually unused, and the 'homeplate_test_suite' advisory lock is per-PostgreSQL-database so it does NOT serialize lanes that override TEST_DATABASE_URL. Concrete sequence: I ran my lane with TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/5; a sibling verifier lane independently chose index 5 as well. Its globalSetup/test helpers issued FLUSHDB and namespace DELs against index 5 while my 200-VU LT-01 gate was running. Observed wrong output: 'LT-01 gate run: ... requests: 437961, errors: 433816, errorRate: 0.99054, errorKinds: {search:401 173156, listingDetail:401 108711, hostPage:401 86644, hostReviews:401 65305}' and the assertion failure 'expect(received).toBeLessThan(expected) Expected: < 0.01 Received: 0.99054' — i.e. the NFR-01 latency requirement appeared to FAIL outright. Diagnosis chain: (1) the same file run alone passed with errors=0 and p95=126.9 ms; (2) instrumenting sessions.getSession showed 296,418 misses whose CLIENT INFO reported a healthy connection on the correct db=5 with no reconnect, yet EXISTS hp:session:<sid> returned 0 — the keys were genuinely gone; (3) `docker exec homeplate-redis-1 redis-cli monitor` during a 25 s probe captured five foreign FLUSHDB commands on index 5 from clients other than mine (e.g. '1786734617.593483 [5 192.168.65.1:48504] "flushdb"') plus foreign DELs of hp:cache:* and hp:ratelimit:login:* keys; (4) `redis-cli info keyspace` / `client list` showed live lanes on indexes 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 9. Re-running the identical lane on exclusive index 14 gave 9 suites / 52 tests passing and a clean 5-minute measurement (0 errors, p95 253.7 ms). Impact: any parallel verification run can fabricate a requirement failure (or, worse, mask a real one) with no warning; Redis-index and bucket collisions are invisible because eviction is off and no error is raised.
findings.proposedFix: Make lane isolation self-verifying instead of documented-by-convention. (1) In tests/helpers/env.js, when TEST_DATABASE_URL is overridden but TEST_REDIS_URL / OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET are not, DERIVE them from the database name (e.g. redis index = hash(dbName) % 16, bucket = 'homeplate-media-' + dbName) rather than silently falling back to the shared defaults, so a lane cannot half-isolate. (2) In tests/helpers/globalSetup.js, after flushing, claim ownership of the chosen index with `SET hp:suite:owner <dbName>:<pid> NX EX <runTimeout>`; if the key exists and names a different owner, abort with an actionable error ('Redis DB index N is already owned by suite run X — pick another TEST_REDIS_URL') instead of flushing another lane's live state. Release it in globalTeardown. (3) Extend the same ownership marker to OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET. (4) Update the CONCURRENCY RULE comment in tests/helpers/env.js to state explicitly that the PostgreSQL advisory lock does not cover Redis or object storage.

findings.title: k6 is not installed, so the NFR-01/NFR-02 acceptance scenario cannot be executed with the instrument it names
findings.failureScenario: `which k6` → 'k6 not found'. The NFR-01 acceptance specifies 'k6 scenario at 200 concurrent virtual users for >= 5 minutes ... reports http_req_duration p(95) < 500 ms', and package.json exposes `test:load` = `k6 run tests/load/smoke.js`, which cannot run on this host. The lane therefore measures with a substitute harness (tests/rt-lt-resilience/lt01-run.js): a Node closed-model VU loop driving the real Express app over real loopback TCP. Two honest deviations from the specified instrument: the load generator shares the Node process and event loop with the server under test (so client-side scheduling delay is folded into the reported latency, making the number conservative but not architecturally equivalent to an out-of-process generator), and http_req_duration is computed by the harness rather than by k6. The measured result meets the budget with margin (791,709 requests, 0 errors, p95 253.7 ms over 300 s at 200 VUs), so this is a provenance gap in the evidence rather than a suspected performance problem — but NFR-01 and NFR-02 cannot be signed off as literal-acceptance passes until it is closed.
findings.proposedFix: Install k6 (brew install k6 — it is free and satisfies the SPMP free-tier constraint) and extend tests/load/smoke.js to the four NFR-01 core operations the acceptance names (GET /api/listings/search, /api/listings/:id, /api/hosts/:id, /api/hosts/:id/reviews) with a 200-VU / 5-minute stage and thresholds http_req_duration p(95)<500 and http_req_failed<0.01, run against a separately started server with the volume seed loaded. Keep tests/rt-lt-resilience/lt01-run.js as the in-suite gate. Record the k6 summary output in docs/verification-report.md alongside the run date and dataset size. Until then NFR-01/NFR-02 latency should stay 'partial' in the report with the measured numbers cited.

lanes.summary: Re-verified ST-01..ST-06 and AB-01..AB-08 against the wave-3 tree by execution, on lane-isolated infra (homeplate_stsec_test / redis db 6 / bucket homeplate-media-stsec) so the concurrent verifier lanes were never queued behind or corrupted by this run. Added tests/st-security/st-security-verify.test.js (33 new tests) to close the gaps the two pre-existing lane suites left: a REAL https.Server started through src/server.js (cleartext bytes on the TLS port, TLS 1.0/1.1 refusal, TLS 1.2/1.3 acceptance), executed proof of logger/validator password redaction, the per-source-IP credential-stuffing counter, injection at the PATCH /api/users/me, POST /api/bookings, search `location` and media boundaries, and a real MinIO put -> deleteForUser -> 404 erasure round trip instead of a spy. Lane result: 3 suites / 98 tests pass (2.9 s), eslint + prettier clean on tests/st-security/. ST-01, ST-02, ST-03, ST-04 and abuse cases AB-02, AB-05, AB-07, AB-08 are genuinely met. ST-05 and ST-06 are partial by wave sequencing: the media-by-key erasure primitive works end to end, but no deletion endpoint, no erasure/anonymization job, no backup-expiry configuration and no CCPA export path exist on disk, and nothing in src/ ever SETs users.deleted_at/anonymized_at or listings.moderation_status — so NFR-12 and the NFR-13 export clause are unmet in this tree. Two reproducible defects found beyond the wave-4 gaps: production config accepts the committed sample FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY and the minioadmin object-storage credentials (defeats NFR-13 encryption at rest for an operator who copies .env.example), and users/repo.serializeUser decrypts unconditionally so one non-canonical *_enc column turns the owner's own GET/PATCH /api/users/me into a permanent 500. The AB-06 OWASP ZAP baseline clause could not be executed — no ZAP binary and no ZAP image on this machine. No application source was modified.

Pre-existing suite adds: buildTlsOptions().minVersion==='TLSv1.2', validateEnv({NODE_ENV:'production',ENFORCE_HTTPS:'false'}) throws, enforceTls() throws when constructed relaxed in production.

findings.title: Production config accepts the committed sample FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY and the minioadmin object-storage credentials, defeating NFR-13 encryption at rest
findings.failureScenario: An operator does the documented thing — `cp .env.example .env`, fill in the live provider keys, set NODE_ENV=production and ENFORCE_HTTPS=true — and the app starts. Reproduced with `node -e` calling validateEnv() on the .env.example values plus NODE_ENV=production, ENFORCE_HTTPS=true, real DATABASE_URL/REDIS_URL, NOTIFICATIONS_TRANSPORT=sendgrid (+SENDGRID_API_KEY/SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL), MAPS_MODE=live (+MAPS_API_KEY), LLM_MODERATION_MODE=live (+base url/key/model). Observed output: 'PRODUCTION CONFIG ACCEPTED with committed sample secrets: FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY = deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef / OBJECT_STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY = minioadmin / SECRET = minioadmin'. Every §3.4 PII column (users.phone_enc, emergency_contact_{name,phone,email}_enc) is then AES-256-GCM encrypted under a 32-byte key that is published in the repository, so 'encrypted at rest' provides no confidentiality against anyone who can read the repo, and the media bucket is reachable with the default MinIO credentials. The config layer already fails closed on every other production-unsafe combination (ENFORCE_HTTPS=false, NOTIFICATIONS_TRANSPORT=mock, MAPS_MODE=mock, LLM_MODERATION_MODE=mock), so this is the one hole in an otherwise consistent guard.
findings.proposedFix: In the production branch of validateEnv() (src/config/schema.js, next to the existing ENFORCE_HTTPS / mock-adapter guards), push a problem when NODE_ENV==='production' and FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY equals the value shipped in .env.example (compare against an exported KNOWN_SAMPLE_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY constant, or reject any key whose 32 bytes are a repeat of a single 4-byte block), with the message already used elsewhere: 'generate with: openssl rand -hex 32'. Do the same for OBJECT_STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY/OBJECT_STORAGE_SECRET_KEY === 'minioadmin'. Keep it production-only so the dev/test defaults keep working. tests/st-security/st-security-verify.test.js already carries the reproduction ('STS-W3-02: production must refuse the committed sample FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY'), written so it stays green after the fix while also asserting that a freshly generated key is still accepted — tighten its first branch to expect(() => validateEnv(productionEnvFromExample())).toThrow(/FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY/) once the guard lands.

findings.title: NFR-12 erasure and the NFR-13 export path are entirely absent: no v1.0 user can delete their account or obtain their data
findings.failureScenario: Executed against the wave-3 tree: DELETE /api/users/me with a valid session returns 404/405 (no handler), POST /api/users/me/export returns 404/405, src/outbox/handlers/ contains only bookingNotifications, bookingPromote, emailVerification and listingGeocode, `grep -rnE "UPDATE users[^;]*SET[^;]*(anonymized_at|deleted_at)" src/` returns nothing, and neither scripts/retention.js nor any BACKUP_RETENTION configuration exists. A user therefore has no way to exercise the NFR-12 deletion right or the NFR-13 CCPA copy right, and the 24-month inactivity sweep and the 30-day backup expiry have no implementation at all. The media-by-key half of the erasure (mediaService.deleteForUser) is built and verified working against MinIO — it simply has no caller. This is scheduled wave-4 scope (U4-PRIVACY), recorded here because ST-05/ST-06 cannot be claimed for v1.0 until it lands.
findings.proposedFix: Wave-4 U4-PRIVACY: (1) DELETE /api/users/me marks users.deleted_at, kills the session, and enqueues an erasure outbox job carrying the user id only (ADR-001 — ids, never PII) with due_at = now() + config.privacy.erasureDays; (2) the worker-side handler anonymizes full_name/email/phone_enc/emergency_contact_*_enc/password_hash on the users row, calls the already-verified mediaService.deleteForUser(userId) for the ADR-004 object-storage half, and rewrites reviews/bookings/safety_alerts to an anonymized author reference while retaining the rows; (3) POST /api/users/me/export enqueues an export job with the same 30-day due date and produces a machine-readable copy of the §3.4 register for the requesting user only; (4) an inactivity sweep over last_active_at older than config.privacy.inactivityMonths that records the notice before erasing; (5) a documented backup-retention control (a scripts/retention.js plus a BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS=30 entry in .env.example) so ST-05's backup-expiry clause has something to review. tests/st-security/st-security-verify.test.js currently asserts the ABSENCE of each of these — invert those five assertions as the acceptance criteria for the wave-4 work.

findings.title: users/repo.serializeUser decrypts unconditionally, so one non-canonical *_enc column makes the owner's own profile permanently 500
findings.failureScenario: Concrete state: a users row whose phone_enc is not a canonical fieldCrypto ciphertext — reachable by a FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY rotation or change (the GCM auth check then fails), by a partially migrated/legacy row, or by the placeholder value 'enc:v1:fixture' that the wave-3 test fixtures themselves use. Reproduced with a standalone script (scratchpad probe, LOG_LEVEL=debug, lane-isolated DB): every PATCH /api/users/me on such a user — including a body as simple as {fullName:'Plain Name'} — returned 500 {"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR"}} with the server log showing 'RangeError: fieldCrypto.decrypt: ciphertext too short — truncated or corrupted at decrypt (src/db/fieldCrypto.js:62) at Object.serializeUser (src/modules/users/repo.js:182)'. GET /api/users/me fails identically. The account is then permanently unable to read or repair its own profile — including the phone field whose absence blocks canReserveSeat — and a key rotation would lock out every user at once. The failure is at least fail-closed: the 500 body leaks no ciphertext, no stack and no internal message (asserted).
findings.proposedFix: Make the owner serializer degrade instead of throwing: in src/modules/users/repo.js serializeUser, wrap each decrypt() in a helper that returns null and logs one warn (module + user id only, no value) when fieldCrypto.decrypt throws, e.g. `const safeDecrypt = (v) => { try { return decrypt(v); } catch (err) { logger.warn({ module:'usersRepo', userId: row.id, column }, 'undecryptable PII column — rendering null'); return null; } }`. The owner then still gets their profile with phone/emergencyContact null and can re-enter the value, while an operator sees the corruption in the logs — which serves NFR-13's 'silent corruption is never acceptable' better than an opaque 500 does. Do NOT relax fieldCrypto.decrypt itself; it must keep throwing. Separately, switch the test fixtures that use `phone_enc: 'enc:v1:fixture'` (tests/st-security/st-security-wave3.test.js and siblings) to fieldCrypto.encrypt('+1415...') so the fixtures stop modelling an impossible row. tests/st-security/st-security-verify.test.js contains the reproduction as 'STS-W3-01 reproduction: a non-canonical *_enc column fails CLOSED on the owner profile read', already written to accept either the current 500 or the fixed 200.

findings.title: AB-06's OWASP ZAP baseline scan has never been run and no CI job or documented procedure exists for it
findings.failureScenario: AB-06's acceptance text requires 'an OWASP ZAP baseline scan against the running app reports no high-risk alerts'. On this machine `which zap-baseline.py zap.sh` reports both not found and `docker image ls | grep -i zap` returns nothing, so the clause could not be executed and is not claimed. package.json has no scan script (only test:a11y uses npx) and .github/ has no workflow step for it, so nothing schedules the scan either — the requirement has no owner and would silently never be measured at wave-7 close-out.
findings.proposedFix: Add a documented, opt-in scan target rather than a new CI dependency: an `npm run scan:zap` script that runs `docker run --rm --network host ghcr.io/zaproxy/zaproxy:stable zap-baseline.py -t https://localhost:8443 -I -r docs/results/zap-baseline.html` against a dev server started with `npm run dev`, plus a README line noting that the dev certificate is self-signed so `-z "-config certificate.allowUnsafeSslRenegotiation=true"` or `--insecure` is required. Record the run and its alert table under docs/results/ as part of the wave-7 measurement close-out, next to the IT-03 results; ST-04's payload suite stays the automated guard in CI.

findings.title: ST-06's two documentation clauses are unfulfilled: the ADR-007 free-tier data-use finding and the volume/disk-encryption deployment note
findings.failureScenario: ST-06's acceptance names two artifacts that do not exist. (1) ADR-007:23 states 'Before any real user content is sent, the team must read Gemini's current free-tier data-use terms and record the finding as part of ST-06'; a walk over docs/**/*.{md,txt} (excluding the SRS/SPMP extractions) found no text pairing 'free-tier data-use terms' with a review or a date — only the ADR restating the open action and docs/verification-report.md:64 deferring it. Since the moderation pipeline will scan private host–guest messages and the §3.4 register lists the LLM API as an external recipient, shipping the live adapter without this finding is a privacy decision taken by omission. (2) ST-06 also requires that 'the deployment note documents volume/disk encryption for the rest' (the data field-level crypto does not cover); `grep -rniE 'disk encryption|volume encryption|at rest' README.md docs/*.md .env.example` finds only the .env.example section header for field-level crypto — no such note exists.
findings.proposedFix: (1) Add docs/results/adr007-data-use-review.md recording reviewer, date, the exact Gemini free-tier terms URL and version read, the verdict on retention/training of submitted content, and which of ADR-007's three options (restrict the demo to synthetic content / pseudonymize before the call / move to a paid tier) the team takes; gate the wave-4 moderation worker's live mode on that file existing, and cite it from ADR-007's status line. (2) Add a 'Deployment — data at rest' section to README.md stating that PostgreSQL and MinIO volumes must sit on an encrypted volume (LUKS/FileVault locally, provider-managed volume encryption in any hosted deployment), that field-level AES-256-GCM covers only the §3.4 PII columns, and that backups inherit the same requirement — which also gives ST-05's backup-expiry clause a documented home.

lanes.summary:
Independently re-verified all eleven binding ADR invariants against the working tree (commit 3136b91 + uncommitted docs). I wrote a new 46-test audit at tests/adr-conformance/verify-adr-wave0-3.test.js that re-derives each invariant with its own probes rather than reusing the existing lane's assertions, and I ran everything in per-lane isolated resources (homeplate_adrconf*_test / redis db 5-7 / homeplate-media-adrconf*-test) so the concurrent verifier lanes could not contaminate the measurement.

CLEAN GROUND TRUTH (excluding the other lanes' in-flight untracked files): 46 suites / 989 tests, 987 passed, 2 failed, 95.1 s. The 45 committed suites / 943 tests all pass; the only 2 failures are my own reproductions of the 2 findings below. A first, contaminated run that picked up the other lanes' half-written files reported 8 failed suites / 13 failed tests - that number is not attributable to src and I discard it.

CONFIRMED FINDINGS (2 major, 3 minor):
- W3-ADR-01 (major, ADR-001): POST /api/media loads src/adapters/objectStorage.js on the request path and constructs an S3Client during the request. mediaService.attach() calls getStorage().assertValidKey(key); getStorage() is a call-time require of the adapter, whose module scope runs createObjectStorage(). No network call happens (proved: attach succeeds in 46 ms with OBJECT_STORAGE_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9), so it is a binding/module-load violation rather than an inline external call - but it contradicts the invariant as written and the module's own header, and it makes the lane's `loadedAdapters() === []` assertions order-dependent (the existing wave-3 lane test only passes because it never exercises POST /api/media).
- W3-ADR-02 (major, ADR-007/ADR-005): the "the automated suite uses the mock adapter" rule is enforced only by a soft default. src/config/schema.js hard-refuses NOTIFICATIONS_TRANSPORT!=mock under NODE_ENV=test (ADR-011, good) but has no equivalent guard for LLM_MODERATION_MODE or MAPS_MODE, and tests/helpers/env.js sets them with defaultTo. Reproduced: NODE_ENV=test + LLM_MODERATION_MODE=live + base URL/key/model yields config.moderation.mode='live' and llmModeration.mode='live'; MAPS_MODE=live yields config.maps.mode='live'. `npm test` on a machine with those vars exported calls the live third-party APIs, contradicting ADR-007 ("only the IT-03 measurement run may call the live API") and burning free-tier quota.
- 3 minor items: an order-dependent maps-cache shape assertion in my own lane file (fixed in place), the one raw SQL statement left in src/modules/media/routes.js, and ADR-009 itself not stating the week anchor.

RESIDUALS FROM THE PREVIOUS RUN, RE-DERIVED AGAINST THE CURRENT TREE - all resolved, none reproducible:
- IT3-F1 (booking.promote re-enqueue dedupe): FIXED. lifecycle.securePromotionSchedule/isLivePendingJob handle the self-dedupe case; my from-scratch reproduction (deliver the promote row early with scheduled_start unchanged) leaves exactly 1 live pending promote row and the booking still promotable.
- ADRC-W3-01 (localDate as a timezone-dependent ISO timestamp): FIXED. serializers.isoCalendarDate emits YYYY-MM-DD; verified equal to the stored SQL DATE on listing create/detail/search/host-page under TZ=Asia/Tokyo, Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14), Europe/Berlin and UTC.
- TCB-01 / ADRC-W3-03 (weekly cap Monday-anchored vs rolling 7 days): the ambiguity is already resolved editorially - requirements-inventory.json FR-11 states "Monday-anchored ... NOT a rolling 7-day window" in the committed baseline, and build-plan flags it for CDR ratification. Implementation matches the authoritative acceptance criteria. I did not silently pick; I report only that ADR-009 (the binding document) is still silent on the anchor.
- ADRC-W3-04 (raw SQL in the media routes file): still present but is a single parameterized, documented wave-4-transitional SELECT - minor.
- COV-W3-02 (dead export listings/repo.toListing): RESOLVED - toListing is used at src/modules/listings/repo.js:144 by findApprovedByHost.
- F-1 (standalone lane scripts bypassing the suite advisory lock): RESOLVED - the only test-DB standalone entry point, tests/rt-lt-resilience/lt01-run.js, calls acquireSuiteLock at line 272.
- MTUT-02 (order-sensitive identity test): out of this lane's scope; not re-derived here.

NOT IMPLEMENTED (wave 4, correctly reported as such, not failures): the ADR-002 two-stage pipeline (no deterministic pre-filter and no moderation.scan handler exist), private-message immediate-delivery/async-scan, and the NFR-12 account-deletion caller for mediaService.deleteForUser (the per-object erasure primitive exists and works against MinIO; nothing in src/ calls it and src/modules/privacy is absent).

NOTE ON LINT: `npm run lint` currently fails prettier on tests/mt-ut-quality/mt01-wave3-audit-gaps.test.js and tests/tc-booking/tcb-w3-reverify.test.js - both are other verifier lanes' in-flight untracked files, not source. My lane (tests/adr-conformance/) is eslint- and prettier-clean.

checks.subject: ADR-001/003 (a) — no external adapter on any Express request path
checks.evidence: Exercised EVERY mounted route (auth/register, users/me, listings POST+PATCH+GET, listings/search, hosts/:id, hosts/:id/reviews, bookings POST+GET list+GET one+cancel, media/uploads, media POST attach, media DELETE) measuring the require.cache adapter delta per route. Output: all routes -> none EXCEPT 'POST /api/media (attach) -> objectStorage.js' (status 201). App boot itself loads zero adapters (passes). Static scan of src/ for module-scope `require('.../adapters/...')` outside src/outbox/handlers and modules/notifications/transport.js: [] (passes).

checks.subject: ADR-005 exception — location search loads only the Maps read adapter
checks.evidence: GET /api/listings/search?location=San%20Diego,%20CA&radiusKm=10 -> 200; require.cache delta for that request = ['maps.js'] only; no sendgrid/fcm/llmModeration/objectStorage newly loaded. Test 'a LOCATION search loads maps.js ONLY' passes.

checks.subject: ADR-001/003 (b) — business row + outbox row commit in ONE transaction (no dual write)
checks.evidence: Row-level proof via xmin: after POST /api/listings the listings row and BOTH outbox rows (listing.geocode, moderation.scan) share a single distinct xmin (Set size 1). After POST /api/bookings the bookings row plus its 3 outbox rows (2x notify.booking + booking.promote) share a single distinct xmin. Both tests pass.

checks.subject: ADR-001/003 (b) — a dual write cannot be expressed; enqueue failure rolls the business row back
checks.evidence: outbox.enqueue(pool) and outbox.enqueue(pool.pool) both reject with /TRANSACTION client|checked-out pg client/. With outbox.enqueue mocked to reject, POST /api/bookings returns >=500, bookings count for the listing stays 0 and listings.seats_remaining is unchanged from its pre-request value.

checks.subject: ADR-003 (c) — outbox payloads carry IDs only, never raw personal data
checks.evidence: Scanned every row of outbox_jobs after all exercised flows: no email-shaped value, no street-address fixture string, and every payload value is a UUID, a SHA-256 hex digest or a short lowercase enum. Unit-level: assertIdOnlyPayload rejects {email}, {note:'reach me at a@b.co'}, {contact:'+1 415 555 0134'} and {fullName}, and accepts {bookingId, event}.

checks.subject: ADR-002 (d) — deterministic pre-filter before the LLM stage
checks.evidence: src/modules/moderation does not exist (fs.existsSync false). The discovered outbox handler types are ['booking.promote','email.verification','listing.geocode','notify.booking'] - no 'moderation.scan' handler. grep -rn 'prefilter|pre-filter|blocklist' src returns only comments in the LLM adapter headers. The two-stage pipeline is wave-4 scope, correctly absent rather than stubbed.

checks.subject: ADR-002 (d) — public content stays PENDING and cannot publish unreviewed
checks.evidence: A freshly created listing has moderationStatus='pending'; to a stranger GET /api/listings/:id is 404, it is absent from search results, POST /api/bookings on it is 404, and it is absent from the host page's exampleDishes. Simulating a provider outage by draining the moderation.scan job with the real registry until the retry budget is exhausted: the job ends status='dead' with last_error matching /no outbox handler registered/, and listings.moderation_status is still 'pending' - never published.

checks.subject: ADR-004 (e) — media referenced by storage key, not bytes

findings.title: POST /api/media loads the object-storage adapter (and constructs an S3Client) on the request path — ADR-001 violation
findings.failureScenario: State: an authenticated host who has minted an upload target via POST /api/media/uploads. Input: POST /api/media {storageKey:'listing/<userId>/<uuid>.jpg', kind:'listing', entityId:'<own listing>', contentType:'image/jpeg', sizeBytes:2048}. Observed: response 201 (correct), but require.cache now contains src/adapters/objectStorage.js, whose module scope executes `const defaultAdapter = createObjectStorage()` and therefore `new S3Client({endpoint, region, credentials, maxAttempts})` — inside the request. Reproduced by tests/adr-conformance/verify-adr-wave0-3.test.js 'every mounted route is exercised and only the ADR-005 Maps read adapter may load', which reports offenders: [{label:'POST /api/media (attach)', newly:['objectStorage.js'], status:201}]; every other mounted route reports 'none'. Cause: src/modules/media/service.js line 60 `getStorage().assertValidKey(key)` inside attach(), where getStorage() (line 44-46) is a call-time `require('../../adapters/objectStorage')`. A standalone probe with OBJECT_STORAGE_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9 shows attach() still succeeds in 46 ms, so no inline NETWORK call occurs — this is an adapter binding/module-load on the request path, not an external call. It nonetheless (a) contradicts ADR-001 as written and the explicit claim in the media/service.js header ('the request-reachable surface of this module keeps no adapter binding') and in media/routes.js ('NO ADAPTER ON THE REQUEST PATH'), (b) makes the existing lane's `expect(loadedAdapters()).toEqual([])` assertions silently order-dependent — adr-wave3-invariants.test.js only passes because it exercises POST /api/media/uploads but never POST /api/media, and (c) puts S3 client construction and credential/config validation on user-request latency.
findings.proposedFix: Stop reaching for the adapter from the request-reachable half of the media service. src/lib/mediaUrls.js already exports the canonical KEY_PATTERN (src/schemas/media.js imports it); add an `assertValidKey` there (or reuse the existing pattern check) and have media/service.attach() call that instead of `getStorage().assertValidKey(key)`. Leave getStorage() used exclusively inside deleteForUser(), which is worker-only. Then either delete the now-stale 'no adapter binding' comments or keep them — they become true. Finally, fold the per-route adapter-delta assertion from tests/adr-conformance/verify-adr-wave0-3.test.js into the permanent lane so the regression cannot come back through a route that the older test never exercised.

findings.title: NODE_ENV=test does not pin the moderation LLM and Maps adapters to mock — the suite can be flipped to live providers by environment alone
findings.failureScenario: State: any developer machine or CI runner that exports LLM_MODERATION_MODE=live together with LLM_MODERATION_BASE_URL / LLM_MODERATION_API_KEY / MODERATION_MODEL (or MAPS_MODE=live with MAPS_API_KEY) — for example a shell left over from a wave-7 IT-03 measurement run. Input: `npm test`. Observed (reproduced with a standalone probe that sets exactly those vars and then requires tests/helpers/env.js and src/config): 'NODE_ENV: test', 'config.moderation.mode: live', 'config.maps.mode: live', 'llm adapter mode: live | model: some-model-id'. The whole automated suite would then call the third-party moderation and Maps APIs. Contrast: the same probe with NOTIFICATIONS_TRANSPORT=sendgrid dies at config load with 'NOTIFICATIONS_TRANSPORT must be mock when NODE_ENV=test (ADR-011)' — proving the intended pattern exists but was applied to only one of the three adapters. src/config/schema.js line 171 computes isTest and line 213 uses it for notifications only; lines 197-198 derive mapsMode/moderationMode from the env with no test guard. tests/helpers/env.js lines 70-71 set MAPS_MODE and LLM_MODERATION_MODE with defaultTo(), a soft default that an exported variable overrides. ADR-007 states 'CI and the automated suite use a deterministic MOCK adapter; only the IT-03 measurement run may call the live API'; .github/workflows/ci.yml sets no adapter variables and relies entirely on that soft default. Reproduced in-suite by tests/adr-conformance/verify-adr-wave0-3.test.js 'NODE_ENV=test must REFUSE a live moderation/maps adapter, as it already refuses a live transport', which currently fails on the second and third expectations.
findings.proposedFix: In src/config/schema.js, mirror the existing ADR-011 guard: after computing isTest, mapsMode and moderationMode, push a problem when isTest && moderationMode !== 'mock' and when isTest && mapsMode !== 'mock', unless an explicit escape variable (e.g. ALLOW_LIVE_ADAPTERS_IN_TESTS=1, added to the schema and .env.example and documented as 'wave-7 IT-03 measurement runs only') is set. In tests/helpers/env.js change LLM_MODERATION_MODE and MAPS_MODE from defaultTo() to a hard assignment unless that same escape variable is present, and extend the CONCURRENCY/adapter note in its header to say so. Keep the escape hatch documented in ADR-007's follow-ups so the IT-03 run records both the model id and the fact that it opted in.

findings.title: The maps-cache shape assertion in the existing adr-conformance lane was order-dependent (fixed in this lane)
findings.failureScenario: The audit at adr-invariants.test.js:273 asserted `expect(Object.keys(item).sort()).toEqual(['areaLabel','lat','lng'])` for every value under hp:cache:maps:*, but src/adapters/maps.js caches TWO shapes: geocode entries {lat,lng,areaLabel} and searchArea entries {areas:[...]}. The moment any earlier-running test performed a location search, this test failed with 'Expected [areaLabel, lat, lng] / Received [areas]'. Reproduced exactly by adding a third file to tests/adr-conformance/, which changed Jest's file ordering: adr-invariants.test.js then ran after a searchArea cache write and failed. No production defect — both cached shapes are public precision. I fixed the assertion in place (it is my lane's file): the audit now flattens entry.areas before checking the geocode shape, so the invariant is checked on every cached area regardless of run order. Re-run: 100/102 lane tests pass, and the two remaining failures are W3-ADR-01 and W3-ADR-02.
findings.proposedFix: Already applied in tests/adr-conformance/adr-invariants.test.js. No source change needed. Fixers should not revert it.

findings.title: One raw SQL statement remains in a routes file instead of a repo (residual ADRC-W3-04)
findings.failureScenario: src/modules/media/routes.js:81 executes `query('SELECT author_id FROM reviews WHERE id = $1', [entityId])` directly inside assertEntityAttachable, rather than through a repo. Reproduced by grep -nE '(SELECT|INSERT INTO|UPDATE |DELETE FROM)' src/modules/media/routes.js — it is the only executable statement (the other three matches are comments). It is parameterized, so NFR-11 is not violated and there is no injection or behavioural defect; the file header and an inline comment already document it as transitional because the reviews module ships in wave 4. Layer-consistency issue only: every other module reaches PostgreSQL through modules/<name>/repo.js.
findings.proposedFix: When U4-REVIEWS lands, move the authorship lookup into src/modules/reviews/repo.js (e.g. findAuthorId(reviewId)) and have media/routes.js call it, then drop the `query` import and the two transitional comments from the header. No action is needed before wave 4; tracked in build-plan §4.

findings.title: ADR-009 does not state the week anchor that the implementation enforces
findings.failureScenario: ADR-009 is the binding decision record for the MEHKO caps, but its decision table gives only 'Meals per host per week: 60' and 'Operating timezone for day/week boundaries: America/Los_Angeles' — it never says whether the week is Monday-anchored or a rolling 7-day window. The implementation (src/config/locale.js comment and src/modules/listings/mehko.js weekRangeFor) is Monday-anchored, and I verified that behaviour end to end. The Monday reading is stated only in the derived documents: requirements-inventory.json FR-11 says 'Monday-anchored ... NOT a rolling 7-day window' (present in the committed baseline — git diff confirms this run did not add it) and build-plan.md lines 243-245 flag it as needing CDR ratification because 'The SRS is silent. A rolling 7-day window is the stricter alternative'. Reporting the ambiguity rather than picking, as instructed: implementation and authoritative acceptance criteria agree today, but the binding ADR is silent, so a future reader of ADR-009 alone could legitimately implement the stricter rolling window and would then contradict the tests.
findings.proposedFix: Amend ADR-009 with one line in the decision table or Consequences — 'Weeks are Monday-anchored on the America/Los_Angeles calendar (a rolling 7-day window is the stricter alternative; deferred)' — and record the team's ratification date, which build-plan.md already schedules for CDR. No code change: src/modules/listings/mehko.js weekRangeFor already implements exactly that.

lanes.summary: Verified IT-01..IT-04 against the tree as it stands (base commit 3136b91, working tree with concurrent verifier edits). IT-01 and IT-02 PASS and were deepened: I added tests/it-adapters/it01c-adapter-depth.test.js (25 tests) covering the Google Places Text Search live branch (previously untested — only geocode had live-shape coverage), the object-storage adapter against the real MinIO sandbox, the LIVE SendGrid and FCM deliver() bodies (previously reachable only through their "not configured" guards), and a two-round regression for the IT3-F1 booking.promote early-delivery bug. Lane result: 4 suites / 69 tests PASS in 3.3 s; eslint + prettier clean. IT-03 and IT-04 CANNOT PASS and no number may be quoted for NFR-10: there is no tests/fixtures/moderation-eval/vN/ set (0 items, 200 required), no results file, no human label sign-off, no ADR-002 pre-filter module, no moderation.scan handler, and no src/modules/safety or safety-alert route — all wave-4 work. I did NOT fabricate a measurement: the ADR-007 mock is a fixture-pattern matcher that scores unseen abusive/scam/spam text as benign 0.99, which I proved executably, so scoring an eval set through it would report an invented FP/FN rate. Of the carried-over findings in my scope, IT3-F1 is RESOLVED (reproduced fixed, including a second consecutive early delivery). Note: the full `npm test` is currently unstable for reasons outside this lane — a run I took mid-session showed 51 suites / 1035 tests with 6 failures, all in test files other verifiers were writing concurrently (st-security-verify, mt01-wave3-audit-gaps, verify-adr-wave0-3, lt01-lt02-wave3, lt-volume-latency) plus one transient failure in tests/adr-conformance/adr-invariants.test.js while another lane was mid-edit on it; that same file passed once its edit landed. My lane is green in isolation and adds nothing to that instability.

checks.evidence: PASS. config.notifications.push.enabled === false in the suite; transport.send channel 'push' → status 'failed', reason 'push_disabled', row last_error matches /push\.enabled=false/, 0 deliveries; fcm.adapter.deliver directly → code PUSH_DISABLED, retryable false (defence in depth).

checks.subject: IT-01 · FCM LIVE deliver() body (src/adapters/fcm.js:89-111) — NEW coverage
checks.evidence: 2 new tests PASS with firebase-admin faked and the gate opened ONLY inside the isolated registry. Message addressed to topic `user-<uuid>` with data {template, params} where params parses back to {bookingId:'b-1'} — IDs only (ADR-003). Error split: 'messaging/server-unavailable' → retryable true, 'messaging/invalid-argument' → retryable false. checks.subject: IT-01 · moderation LLM adapter (ADR-007 mock + live shape)
checks.evidence: PASS. NODE_ENV=test resolves the mock (mode 'mock', model 'mock-moderation-deterministic-v1'). All four taxonomy categories return deterministic {category, confidence, model}. Forced outage → ModerationProviderError MODERATION_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, retryable true; recovery restores classification. Live shape via injected fetch: fenced JSON parsed to {category:'spam',confidence:0.92,model:'test-model-id'}; base URL, model id and key all come from injection (no provider fact in source). checks.subject: IT-01 · object storage adapter against the MinIO sandbox (ADR-004, NFR-09, NFR-12) — NEW coverage

Per-object delete removes exactly that key, get after delete → NotFoundError MEDIA_NOT_FOUND, re-delete is idempotent ({key, deleted:true}), a neighbouring key under the same prefix survives. checks.subject: IT-01 · adapters are worker-only (ADR-001/ADR-003) except the ADR-005 Maps search read

checks.subject: IT-01/RT-01 · NFR-09 degraded path for every adapter named in the acceptance criteria
checks.evidence: Maps (geocode + Places), SendGrid, FCM, LLM and object storage each exercised under an injected outage in this lane, all bounded by the configured per-attempt timeout and retry budget (3 attempts at ADAPTER_RETRY_MAX=2), each resolving to a typed error or a persisted failed row — no unhandled rejection and no bare 5xx in any drill. Search read path additionally returns typed 503 SEARCH_DEGRADED with a user-facing message when no cached area exists (tests/it-adapters/it01-wave3-worker-paths.test.js).

checks.subject: IT3-F1 · booking.promote re-enqueue dedupe losing a promotion (carried-over finding)
checks.evidence: NOT REPRODUCIBLE — the defect is fixed on disk (src/modules/bookings/lifecycle.js:151 securePromotionSchedule, fed ctx.jobId by src/outbox/handlers/bookingPromote.js). My new test forces the promote row due TWICE while listings.scheduled_start is unchanged and still in the future: after each round exactly one pending booking.promote row exists, its id differs from every previously delivered row, and the booking is still 'pending' (not promoted early). Then moving scheduled_start into the past and draining promotes the booking to 'in_progress'. The fix is not single-shot.

checks.subject: IT-03 / NFR-10 · moderation false-positive and false-negative rates < 5 %
checks.evidence: NO MEASUREMENT EXISTS AND NONE CAN BE TAKEN. Executed: fs.existsSync('tests/fixtures/moderation-eval') === false (find over the repo returns nothing); no docs/results or docs/_generated/results directory → no results file, therefore no reviewer name, no date, no set version, no model id (ADR-008 sign-off absent). fs.existsSync('src/modules/moderation') === false; loadHandlers().has('moderation.scan') === false; a walk of src/**/*.js finds no prefilter/blocklist module (ADR-002 stage 1 absent). Item count 0 against the required 200. I also proved the ADR-007 mock cannot substitute: llm.classify() returns {category:'benign', confidence:0.99} for 'You people are worthless trash and should not be allowed near a kitchen.', 'Send $300 in crypto to reserve the whole table, I will refund you after the meal.' and a shouting link-spam string — it is a fixture-pattern matcher with no discriminating power over unseen text, so any FP/FN scored through it would be invented. Reported rates: NONE. Reported as fail-of-bound: NO — the bound was never measured.

checks.subject: IT-04 / FR-07 · safety alert persisted, moderator notified, emergency-contact email delivered, retry exercised
checks.evidence: The FR-07 service layer does not exist. Executed: POST /api/bookings/<uuid>/safety-alerts → 404 and GET /api/moderation/alerts → 404 through supertest (tests/it-adapters/it01-wave3-worker-paths.test.js); fs.existsSync('src/modules/safety') === false; src/routes/index.js names 'safety' in KNOWN_MODULES but src/modules/safety/routes.js does not exist, so nothing mounts. checks.subject: FR-13/FR-14 notification adapters on the booking flow (IT-01 worker leg)
checks.evidence: PASS. booking create → IDs-only outbox rows → worker → one sent NOTIFICATION_ATTEMPT per recipient.
