checks.subject: src/adapters/mockTransport.js (ADR-011 test transport)
checks.evidence: PASS. injectFailures/injectHangs/reset/deliveries() all drive the assertions above; every notification assertion in this lane is made on persisted NOTIFICATION_ATTEMPT rows, never on a third party's behaviour.

checks.subject: tests/fixtures/moderation-eval/vN/ (ADR-008 versioned evaluation set)
checks.evidence: Directory absent (find over the repo, and fs.existsSync asserted in the new test). I deliberately did NOT author a set in this run: with no pre-filter and no LLM stage there is nothing to score it through, and the only available classifier is the mock, so any run would produce provisional numbers against a matcher rather than a measurement. Building the set belongs with U4-MODERATION so it can be scored end-to-end, and it cannot close NFR-10 without the ADR-008 human label sign-off regardless.

findings.title: NFR-10 is unmeasured and unmeasurable: no ADR-008 evaluation set, no moderation pipeline, no human sign-off
findings.failureScenario: Run the IT-03 protocol as specified. fs.existsSync('tests/fixtures/moderation-eval') === false, so the labelled set has 0 items against the required 200; there is no docs/results or tests/fixtures/moderation-eval/vN/RESULTS.md, so no reviewer name, date, set version, model id or prompt version is recorded (ADR-008 sign-off absent); fs.existsSync('src/modules/moderation') === false and loadHandlers().has('moderation.scan') === false, so the ADR-002 two-stage pipeline the set must be scored through does not exist; a walk of src/**/*.js finds no pre-filter/blocklist module. The only classifier available is the ADR-007 mock, and it is a fixture-pattern matcher, not a classifier: llm.classify('You people are worthless trash and should not be allowed near a kitchen.') returns {category:'benign', confidence:0.99, model:'mock-moderation-deterministic-v1'}, as does 'Send $300 in crypto to reserve the whole table, I will refund you after the meal.' and a shouting link-spam string. Scoring an eval set through it would therefore report an invented false-negative rate. Consequence: no false-positive or false-negative number may be quoted for NFR-10 today, and AB-01/AB-04 stay open.
findings.proposedFix: Wave 4 U4-MODERATION: build the deterministic pre-filter (blocklist/regex/rate limit) and the moderation.scan handler that chains pre-filter → llmModeration.classify → moderation_decisions + moderation_queue, keeping public content 'pending' on any provider failure. Wave 4 U4-EVALSET: author tests/fixtures/moderation-eval/v1/ — synthetic, team-written, never scraped, ≥200 items balanced across offensive/spam/fraudulent/benign, with a MANIFEST recording provenance. Wave 7 U7-MODERATION-MEASURE: run the set end-to-end against the live Gemini free tier (the only sanctioned live run), write tests/fixtures/moderation-eval/v1/RESULTS.md with set version, model id, prompt version, per-class counts, falsePositiveRate, falseNegativeRate AND the human label sign-off (reviewer, date), and assert both rates < 0.05. Until the sign-off exists the run reports provisional numbers and does not close NFR-10.

findings.title: FR-07/IT-04 not implemented: no safety-alert service, route, or moderator alert queue — src/routes/index.js names 'safety' but nothing mounts
findings.failureScenario: POST /api/bookings/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001/safety-alerts through supertest against createApp() returns 404, and GET /api/moderation/alerts returns 404 (tests/it-adapters/it01-wave3-worker-paths.test.js, re-run in this lane). fs.existsSync('src/modules/safety') === false while src/routes/index.js's KNOWN_MODULES registry already names 'safety', so the registry advertises a module that cannot be mounted. Consequence: a user in danger has no way to raise an alert; no SAFETY_ALERT row is ever created by the system, no moderator-queue entry is created, no emergency-contact email is enqueued, and safety_alerts.delivery_status never leaves 'pending'. The FR-07 acceptance states 'retrying'/'delivered'/'no_channel' are all unreachable.
findings.proposedFix: Wave 4 U4-SAFETY: add src/modules/safety/{routes,service,repo}.js. POST /api/bookings/:id/safety-alerts must insert the safety_alerts row (booking_id, raised_by, delivery_status 'pending') and its outbox row in ONE transaction and return 201 without calling SendGrid inline (ADR-001). Add the outbox handler that (a) creates the moderator-queue entry, (b) sends 'safety-alert-emergency' through the transport when the user has an emergency contact — set delivery_status 'no_channel' when they do not — and (c) sets 'delivered'; on failure set 'retrying', increment attempts with backoff, and keep the alert listed in GET /api/moderation/alerts even after dead-lettering. Then replace the 404-probe test in tests/it-adapters/it01-wave3-worker-paths.test.js with the real IT-04 (assert on NOTIFICATION_ATTEMPT rows, never on SendGrid). Schema and templates are already in place: alert_delivery_status is exactly ['pending','retrying','delivered','failed','no_channel'], users has emergency_contact_{email,name,phone}_enc, and both EMAIL_SUBJECTS entries render — all verified in this run.

findings.title: Request-path media service loads the object-storage adapter (constructing an S3Client in the request process) only to reach a pure key validator
findings.failureScenario: POST /api/media (src/modules/media/routes.js:118) → mediaService.attach() → getStorage() at src/modules/media/service.js:45 does require('../../adapters/objectStorage') on the request path. src/adapters/objectStorage.js:220 builds `const defaultAdapter = createObjectStorage()` at module load, so the first media attach in a fresh process constructs an S3Client (endpoint + credentials) inside a request handler. No external I/O happens — attach only calls the pure assertValidKey, and the DELETE route merely delete-marks — so the ADR-001/003 behavioural invariant is not broken, but the static 'no adapter on the request path' scan is one refactor away from silently passing over a real inline call, and any adapter-module side effect now runs in request context.
findings.proposedFix: Move KEY_PATTERN/assertValidKey into a dependency-free module (e.g. src/lib/mediaKeys.js) that both src/adapters/objectStorage.js and src/modules/media/service.js import, and keep getStorage() confined to the worker-only deleteForUser path. Then tighten the ADR-001/003 conformance scan so the only permitted src/modules import of src/adapters is src/modules/search/service.js's ADR-005 Maps read.

findings.title: Nothing stops the SendGrid or FCM adapters from calling a live provider under NODE_ENV=test — unlike the LLM adapter, they have no mode guard
findings.failureScenario: Observed live, not hypothesised. While building the harness for this lane I called sendgrid.adapter.deliver({recipientEmail:'guest@example.test', template:'safety-alert-emergency', params:{alertId:'alert-123'}}) inside the Jest suite with SENDGRID_API_KEY set in process.env and the provider SDK NOT mocked. src/adapters/sendgrid.js:29 client() saw the key, lazily required the real @sendgrid/mail, and the process made an outbound HTTPS request to api.sendgrid.com; jest reported 'UpstreamServiceError: SendGrid send failed … Cause: Unauthorized  at node_modules/@sendgrid/client/src/classes/client.js:167:29'. The only thing preventing this in normal runs is that tests/helpers/env.js pins NOTIFICATIONS_TRANSPORT=mock and leaves SENDGRID_API_KEY unset — a per-environment convention, not an enforced invariant. src/adapters/llmModeration.js:190 by contrast resolves the mock whenever config.moderation.mode !== 'live', and src/config's validateEnv refuses *_MODE=mock in production, so the guard exists in one direction only. src/adapters/fcm.js has the same shape (a live path reachable as soon as push.enabled and FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON are set).
findings.proposedFix: Add the reciprocal guard the LLM adapter already has: in src/adapters/sendgrid.js and src/adapters/fcm.js, throw a permanent typed error (e.g. code LIVE_PROVIDER_REFUSED_IN_TEST) from client()/messaging() when config.isTest is true, so a stray key or an accidental direct call can never reach a third party from the suite (ADR-011: 'dev and the whole test suite use a mock transport'). My lane's tests reach the live bodies via jest module mocking in an isolated registry with a hard __fake guard (tests/it-adapters/it01c-adapter-depth.test.js loadIsolated), which would keep working under that guard only if the guard keys off config.isTest rather than the presence of the SDK — alternatively expose createSendgridAdapter({client})/createFcmAdapter({messaging}) factories so tests inject instead of mocking the module.

lanes.summary: Independently re-verified FR-08..FR-14 against the current tree (wave 3 at 3136b91 + uncommitted docs edits). I added tests/tc-booking/tcb-w3-reverify.test.js (28 probes) alongside the 6 pre-existing lane files; the lane is 7 suites / 91 tests, green on 5 consecutive isolated-resource runs, and green inside a full `npx jest` run (54 suites / 1112 tests, 101 s — the 3 failing suites there belong to other lanes' concurrently-edited files, none to tc-booking). Re-derived residuals: IT3-F1 (promote re-enqueue dedupe) is genuinely FIXED and I added a regression detector that distinguishes fixed from broken; ADRC-W3-01 (localDate on the wire) is FIXED for the API but the FR-11 audit records still stamp a locale timestamp; TCB-01 (weekly MEHKO anchor) is a live spec ambiguity that I reproduced rather than resolved — and note the FR-11 acceptance text in requirements-inventory.json was itself rewritten from "rolling 7-day window" to "Monday-anchored" inside build commit 3136b91. Three NEW defects surfaced, the first of which is a blocker: the FR-10 verification email can only ever carry the token DIGEST, so no real user can verify an email (and therefore no real user can become eligible to book); moving a listing's scheduled_start EARLIER never reschedules the booking.promote job; and no template id emitted by any outbox handler exists in the SendGrid subject registry. FR-08 is correctly not_implemented and I proved its safe failure direction (unhandled moderation.scan dead-letters, content stays pending and invisible).

checks.subject: FR-08 (moderation pipeline)
checks.evidence: `npx jest tests/tc-booking` — 'no moderation module, routes, or decision writer exists' PASSES: src/modules/moderation absent, loadHandlers().types() has no 'moderation.scan'. Safe-direction probe PASSES: after 9 forced poll cycles the moderation.scan row is status='dead' with last_error='no outbox handler registered for job type "moderation.scan"', the listing is still moderation_status='pending', GET /api/listings/:id as a non-owner = 404, and the listing id is absent from GET /api/listings/search (200). Anonymous callers get 401 on both read routes.

checks.subject: FR-09 (eligibility policy, both states)
checks.evidence: Restricted: POST /api/bookings by a user with phone_enc=NULL -> 403 NOT_ELIGIBLE, details.reasons=['PHONE_MISSING'], seats_remaining unchanged (2), 0 booking rows. Permitted: after `UPDATE users SET phone_enc=...` the IDENTICAL request -> 201. Publish side asserted in tc09 (HOST_PROFILE_INCOMPLETE -> 201 after profile+agreement). Single-interface grep over all 83 src/*.js files (comments stripped): zero definitions of canReserveSeat/canPublishListing outside src/modules/eligibility/.

checks.subject: FR-10 (registration + email verification)
checks.evidence: Mechanics pass (tc10, 6 tests): 201 + email_verified=false + $argon2id$ hash + same-tx 'email.verification' outbox row; duplicate email -> 409; forced enqueue failure leaves no user row; wrong/reused/expired token -> 400; correct RAW token -> 200 and email_verified=true. BUT the raw token never leaves authService.register() in-process: the outbox payload is exactly {userId, tokenHash}. My probe registers via POST /api/auth/register, reads jobs[0].payload.tokenHash (the strongest value the delivery pipeline can put in the email) and POSTs it to /api/auth/verify-email -> 400, email_verified still false. No resend endpoint exists; users.email_verified is written only by consumeEmailVerificationToken(rawToken).

checks.subject: FR-11 (listing caps, one enforcement point)
checks.evidence: config.mehko = {listingsPerHostPerDay:1, maxMealsPerDay:30, maxMealsPerWeek:60, timezone:'America/Los_Angeles'}, Object.isFrozen true. Only src/modules/listings/{mehko,service}.js reference assertWithinCaps (comments stripped). Literals 30/60 appear in no src file outside src/config/. pg_indexes shows listings_host_local_date_key on (host_id, local_date) WHERE status <> 'cancelled'. tc11 proves 2nd same-LA-day create -> 409 MEHKO_DAILY_LISTING_LIMIT, seatCapacity 31 -> 422, 23:30 PT vs 00:30 PT next day = different days while sharing a UTC day, and two open transactions cannot both commit (23505). Caveat: weekly window shape is a spec ambiguity — see TCB-W3-05.

checks.subject: FR-12 (atomic reservation, AB-02 pending cap)
checks.evidence: seats_remaining=3 with 40 concurrent distinct guests -> exactly 3x201 and 37x409 NO_CAPACITY, seats_remaining=0, count(non-cancelled bookings)=3 (never overbooked). Same-guest CONCURRENCY: 8 simultaneous POSTs on 8 listings with maxConcurrentPending=3 -> exactly 3x201 + 5x409 BOOKING_LIMIT, DB pending count = 3, and every refused listing kept seats_remaining >= 4. Refusal paths write nothing: full listing (409 NO_CAPACITY, seats 0), own listing (409 OWN_LISTING, seats 2), pending-moderation listing (404, seats 4), ineligible guest (403, seats 2) — total bookings across all four = 0.

checks.subject: FR-13 (transactional notification on every state change)
checks.evidence: PASS: create writes exactly 2 notify.booking rows (guest+host) in the booking transaction; cancel writes exactly 2 'cancelled_by_*' rows even under 4 simultaneous cancels; dual-confirmation completion writes exactly 2 'completed' rows. With mockTransport.injectFailures(50) POST /api/bookings still returns 201 in <500 ms, the booking commits, and the failure lands on the worker (jobs stay pending, attempt_count=1, last_error set). tc13 proves a forced post-insert error rolls back booking + outbox + capacity together. Payload audit over ALL persisted rows of ALL types finds no email shape and no PII key. GAP: lifecycle.EVENTS has no in_progress/started member and promoting a booking pending->in_progress enqueues zero notify rows (observed events for such a booking = ['created'] only).

checks.subject: FR-14 (cancellation restores capacity atomically)
checks.evidence: Guest and host issuing 4 simultaneous cancels on one booking: all 200, seats_remaining returns to exactly seat_capacity (4, never 5), and exactly 2 cancellation notify rows exist. Cancel at/after scheduled_start -> 409 CANCEL_TOO_LATE with seats unchanged (3); non-participant -> 403 with seats unchanged. Capacity-shrink interaction probed: 4 seats/2 booked -> PATCH to 2 gives seats_remaining 0, PATCH to 1 is refused 409 SEAT_CAPACITY_BELOW_BOOKED, and a subsequent cancel restores to 1 without tripping the 0001 CHECK.

checks.subject: AB-02 (per-guest concurrent pending cap + audit trail)
checks.evidence: config.booking.maxConcurrentPending = 3 read from config (no inline literal in the service). Enforced sequentially (tc12: attempts 4..20 all 409 BOOKING_LIMIT, target seats untouched at 10) and concurrently (see FR-12 row). repo.lockGuestForBooking uses pg_advisory_xact_lock('booking:guest:'||$1), which is why the concurrent case does not overshoot.

checks.subject: src/modules/bookings/lifecycle.js — IT3-F1 promote re-enqueue
checks.evidence: Reproduction of the original defect state: booking on a listing starting in 2 days, then `UPDATE outbox_jobs SET available_at = now()` on the promote row with scheduled_start UNCHANGED. After one worker cycle the delivered row is status='delivered' AND a DIFFERENT row is status='pending' with available_at exactly equal to scheduled_start; the booking stays 'pending'. Moving the start into the past and firing that surviving row promotes to 'in_progress'. The id-inequality assertion is the regression detector — a naive re-enqueue would leave zero live rows.

checks.subject: src/modules/bookings/repo.js — conditional decrement / cancel / restore
checks.evidence: decrementSeat is the mandated `SET seats_remaining = seats_remaining - 1 WHERE ... seats_remaining > 0` conditional UPDATE; DB backstop tests show a third decrement raises 23514 and seats_remaining+1 above capacity raises 23514. markCancelledBeforeStart returns zero rows on repeat, so restoreSeat runs at most once.

checks.subject: src/outbox/handlers/bookingPromote.js
checks.evidence: Delivered at/after scheduled_start it promotes exactly once; forcing the same row back to 'pending' and redelivering leaves status 'in_progress' (idempotent, RT-02). ctx.jobId is threaded into lifecycle.promoteDueBooking, which is what makes the IT3-F1 self-dedupe detection work.

checks.subject: src/modules/listings/mehko.js — single MEHKO enforcement point
checks.evidence: No cap literal in the file (grep for 30/60 over all non-config src files returns zero); caps read from config.mehko; localDateFor uses Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', {timeZone: config.mehko.timezone}); weekRangeFor('2028-03-12T20:00Z') = {2028-03-06, 2028-03-12} and ('2028-03-13T20:00Z') = {2028-03-13, 2028-03-19}.

checks.subject: src/modules/listings/service.js — update/cancel paths
checks.evidence: PASS: PATCH/cancel are owner-only (403 otherwise); a material edit resets moderation_status to 'pending' and enqueues a fresh moderation.scan; cancel cascades to active bookings and enqueues notify.booking 'listing_cancelled' per guest in the same transaction; capacity shrink below active bookings is refused. FAIL: PATCH {scheduledStart: <earlier>} returns 200 but the booking.promote row still carries available_at = the OLD instant and no row exists at the new instant (asserted directly on outbox_jobs).

checks.subject: src/modules/listings/serializers.js isoCalendarDate (ADRC-W3-01)
checks.evidence: POST /api/listings with scheduledStart 2030-07-09T20:00:00Z returns listing.localDate === '2030-07-09' matching /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/, and GET /api/listings/:id as the owner returns the same string. The previously reported timezone-dependent ISO timestamp is no longer on the wire.

checks.subject: src/modules/eligibility/policy.js
checks.evidence: Sole definition site of canReserveSeat/canPublishListing across src/ (regex over `function can(ReserveSeat|PublishListing)` and `can(...) [:=] (…|function|async)` with comments stripped -> empty offender list). Reason codes surface verbatim at the route (['PHONE_MISSING']).

checks.subject: src/modules/auth/service.js register()/verifyEmail()
checks.evidence: verifyEmail(rawToken) works when given the raw token in-process. register() at line 85 enqueues payload {userId, tokenHash: token.hash} and returns verification.rawToken to its caller; src/modules/auth/routes.js deliberately discards it (comment: 'the raw verification token is deliberately absent'). Net effect measured: the digest is the only token reachable by an emailed recipient and it yields 400.

checks.subject: src/outbox/handlers/emailVerification.js

findings.title: FR-10 unmeetable in production: the verification email can only carry the token DIGEST, so no user can ever verify an email (and therefore no user can ever become eligible to book or publish)
findings.failureScenario: POST /api/auth/register {email:'x@y.invalid', password:'Tcb-strong-pw!42'} -> 201, users.email_verified=false. src/modules/auth/service.js:85 enqueues the outbox row with payload {userId, tokenHash: token.hash} ONLY; token.raw is returned to the in-process caller and src/modules/auth/routes.js deliberately drops it. The worker handler (emailVerification.js:67) forwards params {userId, tokenHash}, and src/adapters/sendgrid.js renderEmail() prints those params verbatim, so the delivered email body reads 'tokenHash: 37c38c33…' with no link and no raw token. Submitting that digest — the strongest value any real recipient can hold — to POST /api/auth/verify-email returns 400 and users.email_verified stays false (reproduced in tests/tc-booking/tcb-w3-reverify.test.js, test 'FR-10 BLOCKER'). There is no resend endpoint and users.email_verified is written only by consumeEmailVerificationToken(rawToken), which hashes its input before lookup. Consequence chain: email_verified can never become true -> eligibility policy always returns EMAIL_UNVERIFIED -> POST /api/bookings and POST /api/listings 403 forever for every real account.
findings.proposedFix: Do not put the token in the outbox payload at all (ADR-003 keeps it IDs-only). Instead have the worker mint or fetch the deliverable link from the token record: (a) add a repo read that returns the verification URL path for a userId+tokenHash (store the raw token only where the mailer can read it, e.g. keep the raw token in a short-lived Redis key keyed by tokenHash with the same TTL as the DB token), or (b) change the token scheme so the emailed value is an opaque single-use lookup id that maps to the hash server-side. Then render a real link, e.g. `${config.publicBaseUrl}/verify-email?token=<raw>`, in src/adapters/sendgrid.js for the verification template, and add an end-to-end test that drains the outbox, extracts the token from the mock transport delivery, and posts it to /api/auth/verify-email expecting 200 + email_verified=true.

findings.title: Moving a listing's scheduled_start EARLIER never reschedules the booking.promote job, so bookings stay 'pending' through the meal and FR-04 completion is refused for both parties
findings.failureScenario: Host creates a listing starting 2031-05-20T20:00Z, guest books (booking.promote enqueued with available_at = 2031-05-20T20:00Z), host then PATCHes /api/listings/:id {scheduledStart:'2031-04-20T20:00:00Z'} -> 200. Querying outbox_jobs shows still exactly ONE booking.promote row, still at the OLD 2031-05-20 instant, and no row at the new instant. lifecycle.promoteDueBooking is self-repairing only for starts that move LATER (it re-secures when it finds the start still in the future); nothing re-enqueues for an earlier start. Consequence: at the real meal time the booking is still status='pending', so POST /api/bookings/:id/confirm-completion returns 409 BOOKING_NOT_IN_PROGRESS for guest AND host. Reproduced in tests/tc-booking/tcb-w3-reverify.test.js, test 'moving scheduled_start EARLIER'.
findings.proposedFix: In src/modules/listings/service.js updateListing, when columnPatch.scheduledStart is set, enqueue a fresh promotion on the SAME transaction client for every still-pending booking on the listing: `for (const b of await bookingsRepo.listPendingForListing(client, listingId)) await lifecycle.enqueuePromotion(client, { bookingId: b.id, scheduledStart: newStart })`. The existing dedupe key already includes the target instant, so the new instant produces a fresh row while the stale row remains harmless (it will find the booking no longer pending, or a start in the past, and no-op). To keep 3A/3B module independence, expose a tiny bookings-side helper rather than importing lifecycle internals, and add the assertion inverted: after the PATCH there must be a pending booking.promote row whose available_at equals the new scheduled_start.

findings.title: FR-13 gap: the pending -> in_progress status transition enqueues no notification at all
findings.failureScenario: FR-13 reads 'When a booking is created, cancelled, OR CHANGES STATUS, the system shall enqueue the configured notification to affected users', and SRS §3.4 gives the lifecycle pending -> in_progress -> completed. lifecycle.EVENTS contains created / cancelled_by_guest / cancelled_by_host / listing_cancelled / completed but no in_progress or started member, and lifecycle.promoteDueBooking calls repo.promotePending without any enqueueBookingNotifications. Reproduced: book a listing, force its promote job due after moving scheduled_start into the past, run one worker cycle -> bookings.status='in_progress' while SELECT DISTINCT payload->>'event' over that booking's notify.booking rows returns exactly ['created']. Neither guest nor host is told the meal window opened, which is also the moment FR-04 confirmation becomes possible.
findings.proposedFix: Add EVENTS.STARTED = 'started' (or 'in_progress') to src/modules/bookings/lifecycle.js and, inside promoteDueBooking's transaction immediately after a successful repo.promotePending, call enqueueBookingNotifications(client, { bookingId, event: EVENTS.STARTED, recipientUserIds: [booking.guest_id, listing.host_id] }) on the SAME client so the transition and its notification commit together. The dedupe key (booking x event x recipient) already makes redelivery exactly-once. If the team decides a 'meal started' email is unwanted, record that decision in an ADR and amend the FR-13 acceptance text — do not leave the requirement's wording and the code disagreeing silently.

findings.title: No template id emitted by any outbox handler exists in the SendGrid subject registry, so every v1.0 email ships with the neutral fallback subject
findings.failureScenario: src/adapters/sendgrid.js EMAIL_SUBJECTS registers hyphenated keys ('email-verification', 'booking-created', 'booking-confirmed', 'booking-status-changed', 'booking-cancelled', …). src/outbox/handlers/emailVerification.js:67 sends template = 'email.verification' and src/outbox/handlers/bookingNotifications.js:80 sends template = `booking.${event}` (e.g. 'booking.created', 'booking.cancelled_by_guest'). The vocabularies are disjoint, so renderEmail() always takes the `EMAIL_SUBJECTS[template] ?? 'Homeplate notification (' + template + ')'` fallback. Reproduced by booking a listing, delivering the notify.booking jobs through the worker, reading DISTINCT template from notification_attempts, and asserting each value is absent from the registry parsed out of sendgrid.js — the assertion holds for every template actually emitted. A guest's booking confirmation arrives titled 'Homeplate notification (booking.created)'.
findings.proposedFix: Make the template id the single source of truth: export the handler-side ids from one module (e.g. src/modules/notifications/templates.js) and key EMAIL_SUBJECTS off those exact constants rather than hand-written hyphenated strings. Add a unit test that iterates the exported template ids and asserts every one has an EMAIL_SUBJECTS entry, so a new flow cannot regress silently. Also note that 'booking.cancelled_by_guest'/'booking.cancelled_by_host' need their own entries, not just 'booking-cancelled'.

findings.title: FR-11 weekly MEHKO window is a live spec ambiguity — the Monday-anchored implementation permits 120 meals in 4 consecutive days against a stated 60/week cap, and the acceptance criterion was rewritten to match the code inside the build commit
findings.failureScenario: weekRangeFor() implements a Monday-anchored America/Los_Angeles calendar week. An eligible host can therefore create 30-seat listings on Sat 2031-03-08, Sun 2031-03-09 (60 seats, week Mon 03-03..Sun 03-09) and again on Mon 2031-03-10, Tue 2031-03-11 (60 seats, next week) — all four return 201. SELECT sum(seat_capacity) over local_date 2031-03-08..2031-03-14 returns 120, i.e. twice config.mehko.maxMealsPerWeek within a single 7-day span. Under a rolling-7-day reading the third listing would be refused. ADR-009 states 'Meals per host per week | 60' and 'day and week boundaries are evaluated in the configured operating timezone' but never names the window shape; the SRS is silent on any weekly cap at all (its AB 626 wording is daily-only). Separately, `git diff af1a91a 3136b91 -- docs/_generated/requirements-inventory.json` shows the FR-11 acceptance text was changed during the build run from '…enforced across the host's rolling 7-day window' to '…the host's Monday-anchored America/Los_Angeles calendar week … NOT a rolling 7-day window' — i.e. the acceptance criterion was moved to fit the implementation. I am reporting the ambiguity, not resolving it.
findings.proposedFix: Do NOT let a verifier or implementer pick. Escalate to the team for ratification at CDR (the working-tree build-plan.md §open-questions already lists this as open question 1). If Monday-anchored is ratified, amend ADR-009 to say so explicitly and keep the inventory text, noting in the ADR's Consequences that the cap is evadable across a week boundary. If the rolling window is ratified, change weekRangeFor/assertWithinCaps to sum seat_capacity over [localDate-6, localDate] and revert the inventory wording; tests/tc-booking/tcb-w3-reverify.test.js 'TCB-01 (SPEC AMBIGUITY, reproduced)' then flips from documenting 4x201 to expecting a 422 on the third listing. Either way the acceptance text must be changed by an explicit decision record, not inside a build commit.

findings.title: FR-11 audit records stamp localDate as a full locale timestamp instead of the YYYY-MM-DD MEHKO calendar day
findings.failureScenario: src/modules/listings/service.js audits `localDate: String(row.local_date)` at three sites (listing.created line ~169, listing.updated line ~384, listing.cancelled line ~441). node-postgres parses a SQL DATE into a JS Date, so String() yields e.g. 'Tue Sep 01 2026 00:00:00 GMT-0700 (Pacific Daylight Time)' — verified directly against the test database. The wire serializer was fixed (serializers.isoCalendarDate returns '2030-07-09'), but the MT-01 audit trail that AB-03 traceability reads still carries an unparseable, host-timezone-decorated string. The sibling mt-ut-quality lane independently fails three assertions on exactly this ('listing.created — localDate equals mehko.localDateFor(scheduledStart) in YYYY-MM-DD').
findings.proposedFix: Replace `String(row.local_date)` with the existing serializer helper at all three call sites: export isoCalendarDate from src/modules/listings/serializers.js (or reuse serializers.publicListing(row).localDate) and audit that value. Do not use mehko.localDateFor(row.local_date) — re-projecting a local-midnight Date into LA time reintroduces an off-by-one on non-LA servers, which is exactly why isoCalendarDate reads the Date's local components.

findings.title: The documented parallel-lane isolation recipe has no Redis DB-index allocation, so two lanes can land on the same index and one lane's globalSetup FLUSHDB silently logs the other lane's test sessions out (spurious 401s)
findings.failureScenario: tests/helpers/env.js tells parallel lanes to set TEST_DATABASE_URL/TEST_REDIS_URL/OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET, and the pg advisory lock is per-database so isolated runs never contend there — but nothing allocates or guards the Redis DB index, and globalSetup unconditionally FLUSHDBs whichever index it is given. Observed on this host: `docker exec homeplate-redis-1 redis-cli info keyspace` reported db1, db3, db4, db5, db6, db7, db9 and db14 populated at once by concurrently running lanes. One tests/tc-booking run on redis DB 5 failed with two 401s (tc09-eligibility 'FR-09 over the REAL routes' expected 201 got 401; tcb-w3-reverify owner-view probe expected 200 got 401) — a session-key miss, since sessions are plain hp:session:<sha256> keys with a 7-day TTL and the only way one disappears is a flush. The same commit passed on db 11/12/13 across five consecutive runs. Attribution to a colliding lane is inferred from the keyspace, not directly observed.
findings.proposedFix: Derive the Redis index from the lane name instead of leaving it to hand-picked env vars: in tests/helpers/env.js, when TEST_REDIS_URL is unset but a TEST_LANE (or JEST_WORKER_ID + project) is set, compute `db = 1 + (hash(lane) % 15)` and record the chosen index in the globalSetup log line so a collision is visible. Better still, stop flushing wholesale: replace globalSetup's `redis.flushdb()` with the existing flushNamespace() over the app's 'hp:' prefixes so a shared index degrades to slower-but-correct rather than silently destructive. Also document in the CONCURRENCY RULE comment that the Redis index — not just the database name — must be unique per lane.

lanes.summary: Independently re-verified waves 0-3 at working tree on top of 3136b91. The COMMITTED test suite is genuinely green: running exactly the 45 git-tracked test files in an isolated lane gives 45 suites / 943 tests passed in 94.5 s (exit 0), and the same set WITH --coverage also passes (96.3 s, exit 0) — so the carried-over finding "W3-F1: npm run test:coverage is RED" is NOT reproducible and should be closed. Measured coverage: statements 92.06% (2889/3138), branches 81.04% (1809/2232), functions 97.21% (488/502), lines 92.94% (2755/2964). 80 of 82 instrumentable source files are loaded by the suite; the 2 that are not (scripts/check-build.js, scripts/worker.js) are child-process-only CLI entry points with spawn-based exercise records. npm run build (83 files parse, createApp() boots) and npm run lint (eslint + prettier) both exit 0. Static stub scan over src/, scripts/, db/migrations: 0 TODO/FIXME/XXX/not-implemented/stub markers. A runtime export inventory (every src+scripts module required, 398 exported names) found no require failures and no exported function returning fabricated data. All 23 mounted HTTP routes were enumerated from the booted app and each is exercised. SRS Appendix B: 17 of 23 named design elements exist as identifiable code; the 6 absent (Review Service, Messaging Service, Safety Alert Service, Moderation Module, Data Lifecycle Service, React Web UI) are all wave 4-6 scope and are correctly declared-but-warned in src/routes/index.js KNOWN_MODULES. Eight findings reproduced, two of them latent suite-reddening defects that the earlier run's list did not contain: a flaky AB-08 security canary that fails on random UUIDs (~1%/run, observed failing), and an ADR-005/010 maps-cache audit that asserts a single value shape while maps.searchArea caches a different one (observed failing twice in full runs; mechanism proved deterministically). Carried findings COV-W3-02 (toListing dead export), COV-W3-07 (.eslintignore), IT3-F2/ADRC-W3-02 (lint), F-1 (standalone scripts bypassing the advisory lock) and the FR-02 host-summary gap are all confirmed RESOLVED on disk. TCB-01/ADRC-W3-03 (weekly cap anchor) is resolved as a documented spec decision, not a defect. IT3-F1 is implemented in src/modules/bookings/lifecycle.js — but its decisive branch is unexecuted by any test. NOTE ON CONDITIONS: other verifier lanes were concurrently adding untracked test files to tests/ during this run; full-tree runs including their files showed extra failures that are theirs, so every number above was measured against the git-tracked file set only, in a per-lane isolated TEST_DATABASE_URL/TEST_REDIS_URL/OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET.

findings.title: Flaky AB-08 security canary: bare substring assertion not.toContain('742') matches random UUIDs in the search payload
findings.failureScenario: tests/st-security/st-security-wave3.test.js:516 'search results are EXACTLY the public allowlist' stringifies the whole search response and asserts expect(flat).not.toContain('742') — '742' being only the STREET NUMBER of CANARY_STREET = '742 Evergreen Canary Terrace' (line 58). The payload also carries randomly generated UUIDs. Observed failing in my run of the 45 tracked suites plus my probe file (isolated lane homeplate_covlane_test): 'Expected substring: not "742"' against results[0] whose id was "24a03a9a-d1d2-4739-9264-6758616742d8" — the digits 742 appear inside the UUID at ...616742d8. No address leaked; the allowlist key check on the preceding line passed and every other canary assertion passed. Rate: a 200,000-trial Monte Carlo over the two UUIDs a single result row embeds (listing id + hostId) gives P = 0.99% per run, before counting the ISO timestamps and numeric fields also in the blob. So roughly 1 in 100 CI runs reddens on a security gate for no security reason, and — worse — the noise trains reviewers to re-run a leak detector.
findings.proposedFix: Drop the bare digit canary and assert against the field that could actually leak. Replace `expect(flat).not.toContain('742')` with a check scoped to string-valued leaf values rather than the serialized blob, e.g. collect the result objects' own string values and assert none matches /\b742\b/ or, better, assert the street number only inside address-shaped fields: `expect(flat).not.toMatch(/\b742\s+\w/)`. The same hazard applies to line 532 `expect(flat).not.toContain(String(listing.lat))` — a short decimal can appear inside a longer number; prefer asserting `found.lat === undefined && found.lng === undefined` plus the existing PUBLIC_KEYS key-exact check, which already proves the allowlist is closed.

findings.title: ADR-005/010 maps-cache audit assumes one cached value shape; maps.searchArea caches an {areas:[…]} envelope in the same namespace, so the assertion fails on suite order
findings.failureScenario: tests/adr-conformance/adr-invariants.test.js:266-278 scans EVERY key under hp:cache:maps:* and asserts each cached object has exactly the keys ['areaLabel','lat','lng']. But src/adapters/maps.js caches two different shapes under that one namespace: geocode writes the bare {areaLabel,lat,lng} (line 298 cache.set of publicValue) while searchArea writes an envelope {areas:[{lat,lng,areaLabel},…]} (lines 362 and 381 return publicValue: {areas}). globalSetup flushes Redis once per Jest RUN, never between suites, and maxWorkers=1 means all suites share that one Redis DB — so the moment any suite that ran earlier resolves a location through the default adapter (e.g. tests/unit/adapter-maps.test.js:514 `await maps.searchArea('gaslamp quarter')`, or tests/tc-core/tc01-search.test.js:74), the audit loop sees Object.keys(item) === ['areas'] and throws: 'Expected Array ["areaLabel","lat","lng"] Received Array ["areas"]'. I observed this failure twice against the full tests/ tree in an isolated lane — once with --coverage (2 failed / 941 passed) and once without (1 failed / 950 passed) — while the 45 git-tracked suites alone happen to order around it and pass. I proved the mechanism deterministically in tests/coverage/cov-verify-probes.test.js: after one geocode + one searchArea the namespace holds BOTH shapes, and a verbatim copy of the line-273 assertion throws on the envelope. Two consequences: (a) any wave-4+ suite that resolves a location silently reddens an ADR conformance gate, and (b) the audit currently never inspects searchArea's cached coordinates at all, so the ADR-010 'a cache read can never leak an exact location' check has a hole exactly where location SEARCH results live. The production invariant itself is intact — my third probe re-coarsens every coordinate inside the envelope and it is already grid-snapped, and the hashed keys contain no address text.
findings.proposedFix: Make the audit loop shape-aware instead of shape-assuming: flatten each cached value into the list of coordinate-bearing objects before asserting, e.g. `const areas = Array.isArray(item.areas) ? item.areas : [item];` then run the existing ['areaLabel','lat','lng'] key check plus the coarsen no-op check over every element of `areas`. That both fixes the order dependency and closes the audit gap over searchArea entries. Optionally also give searchArea its own key prefix (hp:cache:maps:area:*) so the two shapes are separable by key, but the flattening fix is sufficient and keeps a single audit over the whole namespace.

findings.title: IT3-F1 promotion-survival logic is implemented but its decisive branch is never executed: lifecycle.isLivePendingJob has 0 test hits
findings.failureScenario: Parsing coverage-final.json from the tracked --coverage run (45 suites, 943 tests, all passing) for functions with f[k]===0 gives 14 uncovered functions out of 502; the only one in a wave-3 business module is `isLivePendingJob` declared at src/modules/bookings/lifecycle.js:123. Statement coverage confirms lines 124-128 (its body) and line 162 (`return (await isLivePendingJob(client, job.id)) ? job : null;` inside securePromotionSchedule's attempt()) have zero hits, as do lines 230-237 — the `if (!secured)` branch that throws BOOKING_PROMOTE_UNSECURED to fail the delivery so the worker keeps the row pending. Concretely: the tested path is deduped-onto-the-delivering-row (line 161 returns null, then line 169 re-enqueues with the ':r<jobId>' disambiguated key — line 169 IS covered). The UNTESTED path is deduped onto some OTHER row: no test ever produces an enqueue that collapses onto a pre-existing promote row whose id differs from ctx.jobId, so nothing verifies that a spent-or-claimed row is correctly rejected (must return null) versus a genuinely live one being accepted (must return the job). If that predicate is wrong in either direction the failure is silent and exactly the bug IT3-F1 was written to prevent: booking stays 'pending' forever and FR-04 completion 409s for both parties. Equally, no test asserts the fail-closed behaviour when no replacement row can be secured. The carried claim that IT3-F1 is 'genuinely unresolved' is wrong — the fix is on disk with a full doc comment — but its safety net is unverified.
findings.proposedFix: Add two worker-path tests (tests/it-adapters/it01-wave3-worker-paths.test.js is the natural home). (1) LIVE-DEDUPE: enqueue a booking.promote row for (bookingId, startsAt) directly, then call promoteDueBooking(bookingId, {jobId: <a DIFFERENT delivering row id>}) with the listing start still in the future; assert it returns 'rescheduled' and that the pre-existing row is the surviving schedule (no extra ':r' row created), which drives line 162 with a live row. (2) SPENT-DEDUPE: mark that pre-existing row 'delivered' before the call so isLivePendingJob returns false; assert a fresh ':r<jobId>' row is created and status is 'rescheduled'. (3) UNSECURED: make both enqueue attempts collapse onto non-live rows and assert promoteDueBooking rejects with code BOOKING_PROMOTE_UNSECURED so the worker leaves the delivered row pending. No source change is required unless (1)-(3) reveal a defect.

findings.title: ADR-010 precise-location gate: both deny-by-default guards in canViewPreciseLocation are never exercised
findings.failureScenario: src/modules/listings/access.js is the single decision point ADR-010 mandates — its own doc comment says the listing service, host profile, booking payloads and wave-4 moderation views all consult THIS function. Coverage for it in the tracked --coverage run is 84.61% statements / 79.16% branches with uncovered lines 44 and 47, i.e. BOTH early returns: line 43-45 `if (!viewer || typeof viewer.userId !== 'string' || !UUID_RE.test(viewer.userId)) return false; // AB-08: anonymous callers never see precise location` and line 46-48 `if (typeof listingId !== 'string' || !UUID_RE.test(listingId)) return false; // malformed reference`. No test ever calls canViewPreciseLocation with viewer === null, with a viewer whose userId is not a UUID, or with a malformed listingId. Every existing ADR-010 test drives the function through authenticated HTTP routes, which are session-gated and therefore always supply a well-formed viewer — so the anonymous branch is unreachable from the current test surface. If someone later reorders those guards, drops the null check, or lets a non-UUID viewer fall through to the host_id comparison (where `viewer.userId === hostId` with both undefined would return true), the suite stays green while the exact-address gate opens. This is a safety property with an untested fail-closed default.
findings.proposedFix: Add direct unit assertions on the exported function rather than only end-to-end route tests — this is the ADR-010 gate and it deserves a table test. In tests/st-security/st-security-wave3.test.js (or tests/unit/listings.test.js), assert `await canViewPreciseLocation(null, validListingId) === false`, `await canViewPreciseLocation({userId: 'not-a-uuid'}, validListingId) === false`, `await canViewPreciseLocation({}, validListingId) === false`, and `await canViewPreciseLocation(validHostViewer, 'not-a-uuid') === false`. Four assertions, no fixtures needed, and they pin the deny-by-default contract that the rest of the ADR-010 suite assumes.

findings.title: NFR-08 listing audit records emit localDate as a timezone- and locale-dependent Date string instead of the YYYY-MM-DD LA calendar day
findings.failureScenario: src/modules/listings/service.js emits `localDate: String(row.local_date)` in three audit records — line 169 (listing.created), line 384 (listing.updated) and the listing.cancelled record around line 434. `row.local_date` is a PostgreSQL DATE, which the pg driver parses into a JS Date at local midnight, so String() renders the full JS date string. Observed directly in a full-tree run: the audit record for listing.created carried localDate = "Mon Aug 24 2026 00:00:00 GMT-0700 (Pacific Daylight Time)" where the expected value is "2026-08-24". Reproduced for all three events. The module already has the correct helper one file away: src/modules/listings/mehko.js:46 localDateFor() returns exactly 'YYYY-MM-DD' via Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', {timeZone: config.mehko.timezone}), and the stored local_date column value itself is correct — only the audit rendering is wrong. Impact: the NFR-08 record that exists to let a reviewer reconstruct which LA calendar day a listing occupied instead reports the SERVER process's timezone rendering, so the same row audits differently on a UTC CI box than on a PT laptop, and machine-parsing the audit trail for the ADR-009 caps (1 listing/host/day, 60/week) requires locale-dependent string parsing. Note this defect is CONFIRMED present (carried as ADRC-W3-01) and is also covered by the mt-ut-quality lane's own probe, which fails on the same three records.
findings.proposedFix: Replace `String(row.local_date)` with a single canonical formatter at all three sites. Cleanest: have src/modules/listings/repo.js toListing() (and the raw-row consumers) normalise local_date once, or add `const asLocalDate = (v) => (v instanceof Date ? mehko.localDateFor(v) : String(v));` in service.js and use `localDate: asLocalDate(row.local_date)`. Alternatively register a pg type parser for OID 1082 (DATE) that returns the raw 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, which fixes every DATE column at once and removes the Date round-trip entirely — but scope that change carefully since other code may rely on getting a Date.

findings.title: The two production notification adapters' delivery bodies are never executed: sendgrid.js 58% and fcm.js 40% statements, with their NFR-09 retryable classification untested
findings.failureScenario: Tracked --coverage run: src/adapters/sendgrid.js 58.06% statements / 22.22% branches, uncovered lines 37-41 (the sgMail client init) and 98-122 (the whole body of adapter.deliver, including the catch block that derives upstreamStatus from err.code / err.response.statusCode and hands it to UpstreamServiceError, which is what decides retry-vs-dead-letter). src/adapters/fcm.js 40% statements / 5.26% branches, uncovered lines 50-73 (messaging() init) and 91-106 (deliver() plus the TRANSIENT_FCM_CODES 503/400 split). Both files show 100% FUNCTION coverage, which is misleading: only the fail-closed 'not configured' guards run (tests/it-adapters/it01-external-adapters.test.js:366 and the ADR-011 push-disabled check). So the code that classifies a provider error as transient or permanent — the mechanism NFR-09's bounded-retry claim rests on for the FR-13 and FR-07 email channel — has never executed. ADR-011 correctly forbids asserting on a third party's behaviour, but that does not require leaving the adapter's own pure error-mapping untested. Note a concurrent lane has added tests/rt-lt-resilience/rt01-notification-contract.test.js which appears to target this same gap, so confirm before duplicating work.
findings.proposedFix: Test the adapters' error mapping with an injected fake client, no network. For SendGrid, factor the module so the memoised `sgMail` can be replaced in tests (or jest.mock('@sendgrid/mail')), configure a dummy SENDGRID_API_KEY in the test env only, and assert: a resolved [{headers:{'x-message-id':'abc'}}] yields {providerMessageId:'abc'}; a rejection with code 429 and one with code 400 produce UpstreamServiceError with retryable true and false respectively; and that the thrown message never contains recipientEmail (PII register). For FCM, do the same against a stubbed messaging().send with one code from TRANSIENT_FCM_CODES and one outside it, asserting upstreamStatus 503 vs 400. Both adapters stay worker-only and the real transport in the suite stays the mock.

findings.title: src/modules/media/routes.js runs its own SQL SELECT instead of going through a repo, putting DB access in the route layer
findings.failureScenario: src/modules/media/routes.js:81 executes `const { rows } = await query('SELECT author_id FROM reviews WHERE id = $1', [entityId]);` inside assertEntityAttachable, a route-layer helper. Every other module in the tree confines SQL to a repo.js (the file's own comment at lines 29-30 acknowledges this and defers the move to wave 4). Reproduced by `grep -n 'query(|SELECT' src/modules/media/routes.js` -> exactly one raw statement, at line 81. Consequences today are limited — the statement IS parameterized so NFR-11 is not violated, and the surrounding lines 81-88 are among media/routes.js's uncovered statements (88.52% coverage) because the reviews table is empty until wave 4 — but it means the media module reads a table owned by a module that does not exist yet, from the layer that is supposed to do validation and nothing else, and it is the one place a future reviewer scanning repos for SQL would miss.
findings.proposedFix: When wave 4 lands src/modules/reviews/repo.js, move the lookup there as e.g. `findAuthorId(reviewId, {client})` and have media/routes.js (or better, media/service.js) call it. Until then the minimum change is to relocate the statement into src/modules/media/repo.js as a named function so the invariant 'SQL lives in repo.js' holds without waiting for wave 4, and add a test that exercises the attach-to-review authorship rejection so lines 81-88 stop being dead.

findings.title: Nine exported names are referenced nowhere in src/ or tests/ — dead or premature exports that widen the public surface without a consumer
findings.failureScenario: scratchpad/xref.js required all 82 source modules (398 exported names) and grepped every other src/ and tests/ file for each name. After discarding Express router internals (_params, caseSensitive, mergeParams) and names that are used inside their own file, these project exports have ZERO references anywhere outside their declaring module and zero mentions in any test: listings/access.js PURPOSE_SAFETY_ALERT; listings/service.js JOB_LISTING_GEOCODE, JOB_MODERATION_SCAN, JOB_NOTIFY_BOOKING; hosts/service.js EXAMPLE_DISHES_LIMIT; search/service.js DEFAULT_RADIUS_KM; search/repo.js KM_PER_DEGREE_LAT and EARTH_RADIUS_KM; auth/service.js EMAIL_VERIFICATION_JOB_TYPE; notifications/transport.js CHANNELS; config/locale.js regulation; requestContext.js CORRELATION_HEADER; auth/passwords.js ARGON2_PARAMS; schemas/auth.js verificationToken; media/repo.js toMediaObject; and the helper exports migrate.MIGRATIONS_DIR, seed.listFixtureFiles/SEED_DIR, dispatch.DEFAULT_HANDLERS_DIR. Most are constants whose VALUES are covered because the declaring module uses them internally, so this is not a correctness defect — but each is a published contract nothing consumes, and several (PURPOSE_SAFETY_ALERT, JOB_MODERATION_SCAN) are wave-4 anticipations that a reader will mistake for live wiring. I executed the genuinely-callable ones directly to confirm they are not stubs: geoPrecision.defaultAreaLabel, sanitize.escapeHtml, resilience.defaultIsRetryable, dispatch.validateHandler, routes.collectAllowedMethods, eligibility.isHostProfileComplete, users/tokens.generateToken+hashToken and fcm.pushDisabledError all do real work (11/11 probes pass in tests/coverage/cov-verify-probes.test.js).
findings.proposedFix: Two cheap options, pick per name. (a) For constants that ARE the module's contract with a future wave — PURPOSE_SAFETY_ALERT, JOB_MODERATION_SCAN, EMAIL_VERIFICATION_JOB_TYPE, CHANNELS — add a one-line assertion in the owning module's test that pins the literal value, so a rename cannot silently break the wave-4 consumer that will import it. (b) For pure internals with no planned consumer — KM_PER_DEGREE_LAT, EARTH_RADIUS_KM, ARGON2_PARAMS, MIGRATIONS_DIR, SEED_DIR, DEFAULT_HANDLERS_DIR, regulation, CORRELATION_HEADER — drop them from module.exports and keep them module-scoped. Either way the rule to restore is: everything exported has a consumer or a test.

fixerReports.summary:
THREE OF FOUR FINDINGS FIXED IN src/modules/listings/service.js; TCC-04 only partly addressable inside my edit scope.

TCB-W3-02 (major) — FIXED. updateListing now fans a fresh FR-12 promotion out to every still-pending booking whenever scheduled_start actually moved, on the listing update's OWN transaction client:
    if (columnPatch.scheduledStart !== undefined) {
      for (const bookingId of await pendingBookingIds(client, listingId)) {
        await bookingLifecycle.enqueuePromotion(client, { bookingId, scheduledStart: updated.scheduled_start });
      }
    }
- pendingBookingIds is a new private helper in service.js: `SELECT id FROM bookings WHERE listing_id = $1 AND status = 'pending' ORDER BY created_at, id` (parameterized, id-only — NFR-11/NFR-13). It is NOT in listings/repo.js on purpose: the user-focus note flags COV-W3-02 against listings/repo.js and the round's ownership line names only service.js, so I stayed off files another fixer may hold. mehko.js and access.js already carry parameterized SQL in this module, so the placement is consistent.
- I call bookings/lifecycle.enqueuePromotion (the PUBLIC build-plan §3 entry point) rather than re-deriving the promote dedupe key locally. Re-implementing `booking.promote:<id>:<ms>` in a second module is exactly the drift IT3-F1 punished; no lifecycle internal (promotionDedupeKey / securePromotionSchedule) is touched, it is a plain outbox INSERT on the caller's client (ADR-001/003 — no adapter on the request path), and there is no require cycle (bookings imports nothing from listings). I did NOT edit bookings/lifecycle.js.
- The stale row at the old instant is left in place and is harmless (it finds the booking no longer pending, or a start already past). Re-enqueueing on a LATER move too is deliberate: promoteDueBooking's self-repair then dedupes cleanly onto the row created here (verified — rt02-wave3-outbox "start moved LATER" still passes).
- Concurrency argued in the code comment: updateListing holds the listing row lock, and bookings/repo.decrementSeat UPDATEs that same row, so a concurrent booking either appears in this read or blocks and then enqueues against the NEW start returned by its own UPDATE.
VERIFICATION: the verifier's reproduction test (tests/tc-booking/tcb-w3-reverify.test.js, "moving scheduled_start EARLIER") pinned the DEFECT — it asserted exactly one promote row still at the old instant and a 409 BOOKING_NOT_IN_PROGRESS. Per the finding's own instruction ("add the assertion inverted") I inverted it rather than weakened it: it now asserts a LIVE promote row at the new instant, drains it through the real bookingPromote handler, and requires booking status 'in_progress' and POST /confirm-completion → 200. Before the fix it failed with "Expected length: 1, Received length: 2" (proving behaviour changed); it now passes, and the whole file is 28/28.

TCC-01 (minor) — FIXED. hostContextFor no longer emits host: null. When hostsRepo.findHost returns null it falls back to a new non-PII lookup (`SELECT full_name FROM users WHERE id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NULL`), so a live host missing a host_profiles row keeps their name while a soft-deleted account renders hostSerializers.ANONYMIZED_AUTHOR with bio null — deliberately NOT users/repo.findById, which is `SELECT *` and would pull email/phone ciphertext onto the FR-02 read path. Choosing the anonymized name for the deleted case (rather than the verifier's "full_name or ANONYMIZED_AUTHOR") is the NFR-12-correct direction: the fallback must not undo an erasure. The extra round trip happens only on the degraded path. Key set is unchanged (exactly HOST_SUMMARY_KEYS). Both trigger states are now pinned by a new permanent regression test, tests/tc-core/tc02-host-summary-fallback.test.js (2 tests, passing), which also asserts the erased name never appears anywhere in the payload.

TCB-W3-06 (minor) — FIXED. All three audit sites (listing.created, listing.updated, listing.cancelled) now stamp auditLocalDate(row) = serializers.publicListing(row).localDate instead of String(row.local_date), so the AB-03 trail and the wire can never disagree. As the finding required, mehko.localDateFor(row.local_date) is NOT used (it would re-introduce the non-LA-server off-by-one). The three previously-failing assertions in tests/mt-ut-quality/mt01-wave3-audit-gaps.test.js now pass. I also rewrote the stale gap-pinning test in tcb-w3-reverify.test.js ("...String(row.local_date) is NOT a calendar date") into a regression guard: it still demonstrates the String(Date) hazard and now additionally asserts service.js contains no `localDate: String(` and exactly three `localDate: auditLocalDate(` sites.

TCC-04 (minor) — NOT fully fixable inside the allowed file set; documented, not silently dropped. The payload-side option needs keys the service cannot add alone: tests/unit/listings.test.js:463 asserts Object.keys(listing) EQUALS PUBLIC_KEYS ∪ DETAIL_CONTEXT_KEYS, DETAIL_CONTEXT_KEYS is frozen to ['host','reviews'] in src/modules/listings/serializers.js, and tests/tc-core/tc02-listing-detail.test.js:196 hardcodes the same two names — so adding reviewsTotal/reviewsPageSize requires serializers.js plus two test files, none of which are listed in my findings. The spec-side option (state the 5-item preview in the FR-02 acceptance) lives in docs/_generated/requirements-inventory.json, also outside my scope. What I did do in service.js: the module header and the hostContextFor JSDoc now state the contract explicitly — reviews is a bounded PREVIEW of PROFILE_REVIEWS_LIMIT, host.reviewCount is the authoritative total, GET /api/hosts/:id/reviews?page=N serves the remainder. HANDOFF: give TCC-04 to whoever owns src/modules/listings/serializers.js (add 'reviewsTotal' to DETAIL_CONTEXT_KEYS, have the service pass stats.reviewCount through it, update the two key-allowlist assertions), or close it as a spec clarification in requirements-inventory.json.

- npm run lint → eslint clean + "All matched files use Prettier code style!".

- OPERATIONAL NOTE for the report phase: `npm test` finishes the run in ~101 s but then prints "Jest did not exit one second after the test run has completed" and hangs on an open handle (the process keeps only a Redis socket open). That is why a plain backgrounded `npm test` looks frozen with zero output — its stdout pipe fills while it hangs. Redirect to a file (`npm test > log 2>&1`) and read the file, or run per-lane. The hang does not reproduce on any individual lane I ran, and my change adds no new handle (it reuses src/db/pool).

fixerReports.summary:
IT-F2 (FR-07 not implemented) is fixed: U4-SAFETY is built, mounted and exercised end to end.

WHAT LANDED
- src/modules/safety/{routes,service,repo}.js + src/schemas/safety.js. routes.js exports `{ basePath: '/api', router }` and declares its two full paths itself — POST /api/bookings/:id/safety-alerts and GET /api/moderation/alerts — using the same registry fall-through U3-SEARCH uses for /api/listings/search (registry mounts bookings/moderation before safety). Nothing mounts at /api/safety, so the existing "wave-4 surface is unmounted" probes for GET /api/safety and GET /api/moderation still hold.
- POST persists the safety_alerts row (booking_id, raised_by, delivery_status 'pending') AND its 'safety.alert' outbox row on the SAME transaction client, then returns 201. No adapter/transport is imported by routes.js or service.js (ADR-001/003); the tc-core test proves no adapter module loads and no NOTIFICATION_ATTEMPT row is written during the request. Gate: bookingsRepo.findParticipantBooking (the published wave-3 contract) — guest or host 201, stranger 403 NOT_PARTICIPANT, unknown booking 404, anonymous 401, malformed id 422.
- src/outbox/handlers/safetyAlert.js (worker-only, auto-discovered, type 'safety.alert'): (a) emails every Moderator with 'safety-alert-moderator'; (b) decrypts users.emergency_contact_email_enc at send time and emails 'safety-alert-emergency'; (c) marks the alert 'delivered'. No contact (or an erased raiser) -> a NOTIFICATION_ATTEMPT row marked 'no_channel' + alert 'no_channel', never retried. Any failed leg marks 'retrying' and throws so the outbox backs off; on the last attempt of config.outbox.maxAttempts it marks 'failed' and the job dead-letters — the alert stays listed in GET /api/moderation/alerts throughout. All mark* statements are conditional on "not already delivered" (RT-02), and an outer catch guarantees an alert is never left silently 'pending'. Per-leg idempotency keys derive from the alert id, so redelivery reuses attempt rows and sends nothing twice.
- GET /api/moderation/alerts is Moderator-role only (403 NOT_MODERATOR otherwise, 401 anonymous), paginated/filterable, and serialized through an explicit allowlist of IDs + delivery state (no address, name, phone or contact value). It writes no access_log row — src/modules/listings/access.js stays the single writer of that table (ST-06), and it is the listing read, not the queue, that discloses an address.

ONE FILE OUTSIDE MY LIST: src/modules/notifications/transport.js. transport.send() resolved the recipient address from the RECIPIENT USER's account, so FR-07 would have emailed the person in danger instead of their emergency contact in live mode. I added an optional, backward-compatible `recipientEmail` input (validated, handed straight to the adapter, never persisted or logged; the attempt row still carries recipient_user_id only). This is additive and coexists with the FR-10 `resolveRenderContext` change another fixer made to the same file concurrently.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE PROPOSED FIX: the worker does NOT insert a moderation_queue row. That table's content_type enum is ('listing','review','message') — FR-08 content review — and db/migrations/0006_moderation_queue.sql belongs to U4-MODERATION; migrations are append-only so 0001 was not touched. The safety_alerts row itself is the FR-07 queue entry (visible at GET /api/moderation/alerts from the instant the request commits, i.e. review never waits on delivery), and the worker's moderator email is the push half of "notify the moderator". This is documented in service.js. If U4-MODERATION later defines its own /alerts route it will shadow this one (mount order) — flagged in routes.js so the next agent sees it.

TESTS: added tests/unit/safety.test.js, tests/tc-core/tc07-safety.test.js, tests/it-adapters/it04-safety-delivery.test.js (24 tests: happy path, redelivery no-op, no_channel, injected outage -> retrying + still queued -> recovery reuses the same attempt row, budget exhaustion -> dead letter + 'failed' + still listed, and proof the adapter received the CONTACT's address and not the raiser's own). Updated 6 stale wave-3 scope guards that asserted the FR-07 gap (their own headers instructed this when the module landed): the it01 404 probe, it01c "write path does not exist", the tc05-07 TC-07 probe, the coverage-lane and st-security-verify module-absence lists, and the adr-invariants exact transport-importer list (now includes handlers/safetyAlert.js — still only outbox handlers).

fixerReports.summary:
IT-F1 is correct and reproduced, but it is three separate gaps and only one of them is closable in this round. I closed that one — the ADR-008 evaluation set, which is the file set I own — and left the other two open with evidence rather than faking them.

WHAT I BUILT (tests/fixtures/moderation-eval/)

1. `v1/` — the ADR-008 set. 224 synthetic items, exactly balanced (56 offensive / 56 spam / 56 fraudulent / 56 benign; SRS §4.2 floor is 200), spread across all four v1.0 surfaces (listing, review, message, profile). Every item is written for this repo — never scraped, no third-party corpus, no personal data: all domains are `.example`, all phone numbers are in the reserved 555-01xx range, and a test asserts both. 31 of the 56 benign items are deliberate hard negatives (7 negative reviews, 5 safety/allergen reports, 3 that quote the abuse they are reporting, 4 legitimate cash arrangements, 2 non-English, 11 lexical look-alikes like "this dish is killer", "free parking", "wire rack", "a gift card for the market"). Without those the false-positive rate is unmeasurable, and moderating them away is exactly the failure NFR-10 bounds.
   `v1/MANIFEST.md` + `v1/manifest.json` record provenance, the four-class taxonomy, and four boundary rules that make the hard cases decidable for the human reviewer: dominant-violation ordering (offensive > fraudulent > spam), spam = untargeted promotion vs fraudulent = deceiving a specific person out of money/credentials/documents, "payments are out of v1.0 scope so cash-on-the-night is benign but an upfront transfer/gift-card/crypto demand is fraud", and "criticism is benign".

2. `index.js` — loader, validator, scorer and claim gate. It fixes the operational definition NFR-10 was missing: FP = benign item put in any violating class (/56 benign), FN = violating item classified benign (/168 violating), plus a `misrouted` count for violating-to-wrong-violating (not an FP or FN under the binary bound, but FR-08 routes on it). `validateSet()` enforces the whole ADR-008 contract (>=200, balance within 10%, unique ids and texts, synthetic/never-scraped/no-PII provenance, sign-off block shape). `claimability()` refuses to certify an NFR-10 pass unless there is (a) a recorded human sign-off with reviewer+date+set version and (b) a live, non-mock model id and a prompt version.

3. `set-integrity.test.js` — 13 tests, all passing, covering the structure, the metric arithmetic (perfect run = 0/0; a crafted 3-FP/2-FN/1-misroute run scores exactly that and 3/56 = 5.36% correctly reads as OVER the bound), the error paths (partial/foreign/off-taxonomy predictions cannot yield a rate), and both gates including the negative control that the gate is not unconditionally closed.

THE MOCK-CLASSIFIER LEG — deliberately NOT "fixed"
The finding is right that `llm.classify('You people are worthless trash...')` returns benign/0.99. I did not touch `src/adapters/llmModeration.mock.js`: teaching the mock to classify this corpus correctly is precisely what ADR-008 rejects ("measuring a classifier against its own output is not a measurement"), and ADR-007 requires the mock to be deterministic for CI, not accurate. The real fix is to make a mock-derived number unreportable, which is now enforced in code. Measured: scoring the set through the mock gives falseNegativeRate 0.9643 (162/168) and falsePositives 2 — `ben-006` ("a guest called me an idiot", a report of abuse) and `ben-046` ("a gift card for the Asian market") — and `claimability()` returns claimable:false on two independent grounds. That FP=2/56=3.57% would have read as "inside the 5% bound" if anyone had quoted it; it now cannot be.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN (why IT-F1 is unresolved, not resolved)
- The ADR-002 pipeline: `src/modules/moderation/` and the `moderation.scan` handler still do not exist. That is wave-4 U4-MODERATION, it is not code I own this round, and other fixers are actively writing in src/ right now. Verified still absent.
- The ADR-008 human label sign-off: `labelReview.status = "unreviewed"`, reviewer and date `null`, no `v1/RESULTS.md`. I did not fabricate one. ADR-008 line 30 is explicit that this control "cannot itself be delegated to an agent", so an agent-written sign-off would defeat the requirement rather than satisfy it. Any IT-03 run before it lands reports provisional numbers only.
- The live measurement: ADR-007 sanctions exactly one live-provider run, in wave 7 (U7-MODERATION-MEASURE).
So NFR-10 stays not_implemented and AB-01/AB-04 stay open, exactly as the finding says. What changed is that the corpus, the metric definitions and the refusal-to-claim are now on disk and under test, so wave 4/7 only has to build the pipeline and run it.

TWO EDITS OUTSIDE THE FINDING'S FILE LIST — flagging explicitly
Two verifier-written probes asserted `fs.existsSync('tests/fixtures/moderation-eval') === false`, so creating the set would have turned the suite red on files I was not given:
- tests/it-adapters/it01c-adapter-depth.test.js:699
- tests/it-adapters/it01-wave3-worker-paths.test.js:595
Both carry comments saying they FAIL BY DESIGN once the gap closes. I did not delete or weaken them: I advanced each to assert the remaining gap instead of the closed one — the set now exists AND conforms (validateSet == []), AND there is still no RESULTS.md, no reviewer, no date, no `moderation.scan` handler, and `claimability()` refuses even a live model id. They guard the same property (no NFR-10 claim is possible) with strictly more assertions. Both pass. If another fixer owns those files, this is the change to reconcile.

I also refreshed the NFR-10 row of docs/verification-report.md. Note the report on disk had already been updated to waves 0–3 and already said "No number may be quoted for NFR-10 today" — that sub-claim of the finding was satisfied before I started; I only corrected the now-stale "no ADR-008 evaluation set" clause and added the eval-set evidence while keeping the NOT IMPL verdict.

VERIFICATION / CONCURRENCY CAVEAT
`npm test` in the shared lane queued behind 9 concurrent jest runs from other fixers, so I ran in an isolated lane (TEST_DATABASE_URL=...homeplate_evalset_test, TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/9, OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET=homeplate-media-evalset-test; lane DB dropped afterwards). Zero failures reference moderation-eval; `grep moderation-eval full-run.log` returns only the PASS line. eslint and prettier are clean on every file I touched; `npm run build` passes (88 files, createApp() boots). The suite-wide gate needs re-measuring by the report phase once the tree quiesces — and note jest now prints "did not exit one second after the test run has completed", an open-handle regression that appeared with the concurrent wave-4 work, not with this change.

fixerReports.summary:
TCB-W3-01 (FR-10 blocker) is fixed at the cause, with every ADR invariant intact.

ROOT CAUSE. The raw token is unrecoverable after register() by design — PostgreSQL keeps only the SHA-256 digest (users/tokens.js) and ADR-003 forbids putting the raw token in the outbox payload — so the delivery pipeline had nothing mailable and printed `tokenHash: …`. A digest is not a credential, so the loop could never close.

FIX. The worker now mints the deliverable link at delivery time and hands it to the mail adapter as per-send, never-persisted "render context" — the same seam through which the FR-07 recipientEmail already reaches an adapter without touching a row:
- src/modules/auth/service.js: new `createVerificationLink(userId, {log})` (worker-side, ADR-006 auth service owns tokens). One transaction mints a fresh single-use token and returns `${config.server.publicBaseUrl}/api/auth/verify-email?token=<raw>`. The raw value lives only in worker memory and the outgoing email — never in a payload, row, log line or Redis. register() is unchanged.
- src/outbox/handlers/emailVerification.js: passes `resolveRenderContext` to transport.send. Payload and notification params stay exactly {userId, tokenHash}.
- src/modules/notifications/transport.js: resolves the render context ONCE, after the dedupe and push-gate returns and only for an adapter declaring `requiresRenderContext`, then hands it to adapter.deliver. Never persisted, never logged. Because the ADR-011 mock does not declare it, dev/test mint no credentials at all.
- src/adapters/sendgrid.js: `requiresRenderContext: true`; renderEmail(template, params, renderContext) renders the real link + single-use/expiry note; both template spellings ('email.verification' from the handler, 'email-verification' in the subject registry) now resolve to the verification subject instead of the neutral fallback; deliver() REFUSES a verification send with no link (SENDGRID_NO_VERIFICATION_LINK, non-retryable) rather than mailing an empty one.
- src/config/schema.js + .env.example: new PUBLIC_BASE_URL → config.server.publicBaseUrl (required and https-only in production, `https://localhost:${PORT}` elsewhere). A link needs a real origin; guessing one would ship a known-wrong value.

FAILURE SCENARIO NO LONGER REPRODUCES. New tests/tc-booking/fr10-verification-link.test.js (7 tests) registers over HTTP, runs the REAL handler and REAL transport, captures what the mail adapter receives, extracts the token from the link (and separately from the rendered SendGrid body), and gets 200 {emailVerified:true} with users.email_verified=true and can_reserve_seat=true; the digest still (correctly) returns 400; the link is absent from the outbox payload, the NOTIFICATION_ATTEMPT row and the token table; replay is 400.

VERIFICATION. npm run build: all checks pass (88 files parse, createApp boots against .env.example). npm run lint: eslint + prettier clean across the whole tree. Full suite in an isolated lane (TEST_DATABASE_URL/TEST_REDIS_URL/OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET per lane, since other fixers were running concurrently): 60 suites / 1158 tests, 101.9 s — 1 suite / 2 tests failing, both PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to this fix (evidence below). Targeted rerun of the FR-10 blast radius (fr10-verification-link, tcb-w3-reverify, it02, tc10, identity, config, adapters-comms): 7 suites / 147 tests, all pass — including tcb-w3-reverify's characterization tests, which I did not weaken: the digest still fails, and sendgrid.js still contains no `'email.verification':` registry key.

THE 2 REMAINING FAILURES ARE NOT MINE (both in tests/adr-conformance/verify-adr-wave0-3.test.js):
(a) "adapter purity across the FULL mounted route surface" — POST /api/media (attach) loads objectStorage.js on the request path via the call-time require at src/modules/media/service.js:45. My diff touches no media code and adds no adapter to any request path.
(h) "NODE_ENV=test must REFUSE a live moderation/maps adapter" — src/config/schema.js still has an isTest guard only for NOTIFICATIONS_TRANSPORT. Proved independent by running HEAD's schema.js and the working-tree schema.js side by side on the same env: both return "NO THROW". My schema edit is additive and only concerns PUBLIC_BASE_URL.
(An earlier full run also showed 2 failures in tests/unit/hosts-media.test.js and elsewhere that disappeared in the next run — other fixers were editing the shared tree mid-run.)

SCOPE DEVIATION (disclosed). The finding listed 4 files. src/modules/auth/routes.js needed NO change — dropping the raw token from the 201 response is exactly what FR-10 requires, and tests assert the response carries no token. I did have to touch 2 files outside the list: transport.js (the only seam that can carry per-send secret material to an adapter without persisting it — putting the link in `params` would have violated ADR-003 and broken four existing tests that pin the persisted key set) and config/schema.js/.env.example (a production-correct link needs a configured origin). All edits were surgical string replacements, never whole-file writes, so concurrent fixers' work in the same tree is preserved.

RESIDUAL OBSERVATIONS (not fixed, outside FR-10 acceptance / my file scope):
1. Still no resend endpoint: if a verification job dead-letters, the account has no way to request a new link. Would need src/schemas/auth.js + routes.js.
2. In production each actually-mailed verification email mints its own token row; the registration-time token is never mailed. All rows are single-use and expire with EMAIL_TOKEN_TTL_HOURS — a bounded, documented cost of keeping the raw token out of every store.
3. Jest hangs after the suite reports results (open handle — an idle ioredis connection); `--forceExit` or a leak fix would save minutes per run. This is global, not introduced here.

I booted the real app and walked the Express routing table and outbox registry rather than trusting greps. Script: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gaetan-Desktop-MSCS-Software-Engineer-HomePlate/cde758fc-0771-4d1d-91a9-c92af4c5810c/scratchpad/probe-privacy.js

  /api/users/me/export     -> (no route: 404)
  /api/privacy             -> (no route: 404)
