Plus: `grep -rnE "UPDATE users[^;]*SET[^;]*(anonymized_at|deleted_at)" src/` exits 1; scripts/retention.js and scripts/backup.js absent; no BACKUP_RETENTION in .env.example. Every clause of the finding holds.

Two corrections/refinements to the finding's wording:
1. It says DELETE/POST return "404/405" — measured, they are specifically 405 with an `Allow: GET, HEAD, PATCH` header (the path is known, the verbs are not). `/api/users/me/export` is a true 404. Both satisfy the existing test's `[404,405]` assertion.
2. `users.deleted_at` and `users.anonymized_at` already exist in db/migrations/0001_core_schema.sql (lines 95-96) and `last_active_at` at line 94, and `config.privacy.erasureDays=30` / `inactivityMonths=24` already exist in src/config/schema.js. The schema and config half of NFR-12 is in place; only the behaviour is missing. `mediaService.deleteForUser` (src/modules/media/service.js:124) is built and MinIO-verified but has ZERO production callers — the only references outside its own definition are a comment in src/modules/media/routes.js:14 and tests.

WHY I DID NOT IMPLEMENT IT (not a refusal to work — a correctness judgement)
- Ownership: I own only src/modules/users/routes.js. A correct U4-PRIVACY needs users/service.js, users/repo.js, src/config/schema.js, .env.example and a 0005 migration for the export-request row. `git status` shows .env.example and src/config/schema.js are being edited by concurrent fixers right now, so touching them would collide.
- Any version confined to routes.js requires raw SQL and a transaction opened inside a request handler. That is precisely the ADRC-W3-04 anti-pattern already recorded against src/modules/media/routes.js — I would be fixing one finding by creating another.
- Half-landing it is worse than not landing it. A DELETE /api/users/me that marks deleted_at and enqueues an `account.erasure` job with no registered handler would dead-letter every erasure: the user sees "account deleted", the PII and the object-storage media survive. That is a placeholder implementation and a privacy regression, both explicitly forbidden.
- The five ST-05/ST-06 assertions in tests/st-security/st-security-verify.test.js (lines 509, 518, 527, 537, 722) assert the ABSENCE of this surface and are green today. They must flip to their inverted form in the SAME change that lands the feature, or the suite goes red. That test file is untracked/new and outside my file list — inverting it unilaterally while another agent may own it would be exactly the "change the test to go green" move the rules prohibit.
- The finding itself already classifies this as "scheduled wave-4 scope (U4-PRIVACY), recorded here because ST-05/ST-06 cannot be claimed for v1.0 until it lands." Nothing in wave-3 code is defective; this is a scope gap.

HANDOFF SPEC for whoever owns U4-PRIVACY (one atomic change across all files)
1. New module src/modules/privacy/{routes,service,repo}.js exporting `{ basePath: '/api/users', router }` so it mounts alongside the users router without editing src/routes/index.js — 'privacy' is already in KNOWN_MODULES (src/routes/index.js:41) and the registry's `{basePath, router}` contract supports this. This keeps users/routes.js untouched and avoids two units editing one file.
2. DELETE /api/users/me: inside ONE withTransaction — set users.deleted_at, insert the outbox row (payload = `{userId}` only, ADR-001 ids-never-PII), destroy the Redis session; due_at = now() + config.privacy.erasureDays.
3. src/outbox/handlers/accountErasure.js (worker-only): anonymize full_name/email/password_hash/phone_enc/emergency_contact_*_enc, set anonymized_at, call the already-verified mediaService.deleteForUser(userId) for the ADR-004 half, and repoint reviews/bookings/safety_alerts at an anonymized author reference while retaining the rows. This handler is the ONLY place the object-storage adapter is reached.
4. POST /api/users/me/export enqueues an export job producing the §3.4 register for the requesting user only; delivery via object storage + an ADR-011 SendGrid link, both worker-side.
5. Inactivity sweep over last_active_at > config.privacy.inactivityMonths that records the notice before erasing.
6. scripts/retention.js + BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS=30 in .env.example and src/config/schema.js so ST-05's backup-expiry clause has a reviewable control.
7. In the same commit, invert the five assertions at tests/st-security/st-security-verify.test.js:509, 518, 527, 537, 722.

fixerReports.summary:
TCB-W3-05 is confirmed and correctly diagnosed, and I deliberately did NOT resolve it in code. The finding itself says an implementer must not pick a reading, and picking one is impossible for a fixer anyway: the Monday anchor is pinned by three test files I do not own (tests/unit/listings.test.js, tests/tc-booking/tc11-listing-caps.test.js, tests/tc-booking/tcb-w3-reverify.test.js), so "fixing" it in mehko.js would mean rewriting the tests that document it — exactly the move the finding condemns.

REPRODUCED. mehko.weekRangeFor puts 2031-03-08 (Sat) and 03-09 (Sun) in week 2031-03-03..03-09 and 2031-03-10 (Mon) and 03-11 (Tue) in week 03-10..03-16, so four 30-seat listings on four consecutive days all pass assertWithinCaps: 120 seats inside the 7-day span 03-08..03-14 against a 60/week cap. The provenance claim also checks out — `git diff af1a91a 3136b91 -- docs/_generated/requirements-inventory.json` shows the FR-11 acceptance text changed from "…enforced across the host's rolling 7-day window" to "…Monday-anchored … NOT a rolling 7-day window" inside build commit 3136b91. The SRS is genuinely silent (its AB 626 wording at §2.1.7/§3.4/FR-11 is daily-only; it states no weekly cap at all), and ADR-009 fixed the number and the timezone but never the window shape. So the requirement really was defined by the implementation.

WHAT I FIXED — the process defect, which is the actionable half:
1. ADRs/# ADR-009: Status now reads "Accepted — with one open sub-decision"; new section "Weekly window shape — OPEN, not ratified" tabulating both readings, stating that the Monday anchor is an implementation default rather than a decision, and spelling out both ratification paths (under the rolling reading, exactly which function changes and which three test files flip to expect 422). The rolling window is added to Alternatives considered as explicitly *not decided either way*, not as rejected. A new Consequences bullet quantifies the residual risk with the worked 120-meals example. An Amendment log records that the acceptance criterion was moved to fit the code inside 3136b91, that this amendment resolves nothing, and that CDR ratification is required.

STS-W3-02 (production accepted committed sample secrets). validateEnv() now fails closed in the production branch, beside the existing ENFORCE_HTTPS/mock-adapter guards: (a) FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY is rejected when it is a placeholder — implemented as isPlaceholderHexKey(), which rejects any 64-hex value that is one short block repeated (catches the committed 'deadbeef'x8, '00'x32, 'ab'x32, and near-miss variants), with the message ending 'generate with: openssl rand -hex 32'; (b) OBJECT_STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY / OBJECT_STORAGE_SECRET_KEY are rejected when equal to the documented MinIO default 'minioadmin' (ADR-004, AB-08). KNOWN_SAMPLE_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY, DEFAULT_OBJECT_STORAGE_CREDENTIALS and isPlaceholderHexKey are exported so tests assert one definition. Reproduction before: 'PRODUCTION CONFIG ACCEPTED with committed sample secrets: FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY = deadbeef… / OBJECT_STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY = minioadmin / SECRET = minioadmin'. After: three problems raised, start-up refused; a freshly generated key plus real storage credentials still validates.

W3-ADR-02 (NODE_ENV=test could be flipped to live adapters). Mirroring the existing ADR-011 transport guard: under NODE_ENV=test, LLM_MODERATION_MODE != mock and MAPS_MODE != mock are now config errors unless the new ALLOW_LIVE_ADAPTERS_IN_TESTS=true escape hatch is set (documented in .env.example as wave-7 IT-03 measurement runs only). tests/helpers/env.js now HARD-assigns NOTIFICATIONS_TRANSPORT/MAPS_MODE/LLM_MODERATION_MODE to mock instead of defaultTo() (defaultTo is overridden by an exported shell variable — the actual defect), keeping defaultTo only inside the IT-03 opt-in branch; its header CONCURRENCY/adapter note documents this. The opt-in never relaxes ADR-011 (verified: transport still hard-refused with the hatch on) and grants nothing in production. Reproduction probe before: 'config.moderation.mode: live / config.maps.mode: live'; after: both 'mock'.

No ADR invariant was weakened: nothing new is called from a request handler, no adapter moved out of the worker, and the mock-only rule for CI is now enforced by code rather than by a soft default.

Two consequential test-file edits, both fixture corrections rather than weakened assertions. (1) tests/unit/config.test.js: its 'production-shaped environment' fixture spread .env.example verbatim, so it carried the sample key and minioadmin — no longer production-shaped once the guard lands. It now supplies real generated credentials, and I added 8 tests covering both new guards (sample key refused, repeated-block keys refused, fresh key accepted, MinIO defaults refused, dev/test unaffected, live modes refused under NODE_ENV=test, the IT-03 opt-in, and that the opt-in does not relax ADR-011). (2) tests/st-security/st-security-verify.test.js: tightened exactly as the finding instructed — the first branch is now expect(...).toThrow(/FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY/) instead of the try/catch reproduction, plus an assertion that the storage credentials are refused too, and the 'fresh key is still accepted' branch now supplies real storage credentials as well (otherwise it would have asserted that minioadmin is acceptable in production).

Environment note on the full-suite run. The shared working tree is being edited by other fixers concurrently (safety module, notifications transport, sendgrid/fcm adapters, auth service, listings service). A full `npm test` in an isolated lane gave 60 suites / 1166 tests with 6 failures: rt01-degradation, tc13-notifications, rt02-wave3-outbox, unit/listings (FR-09 eligibility) and two ST-04 injection tests in st-security-verify. Incidental observation worth passing to whoever owns the outbox: src/outbox/worker.js line 129 computes the retry deadline as `available_at = now() + delay`, and PostgreSQL now() is transaction-start time, so a poll cycle whose batch takes longer than OUTBOX_BACKOFF_BASE_MS schedules a retry in the past — that is what makes rt01-degradation/tc13 fail against a dirty or slow lane database. MTUT-W3-01 and COV-05 are the same defect (both cite `String(row.local_date)` at the three listing audit sites). Both are CONFIRMED real against HEAD 3136b91 and both are already FIXED in the working tree — I made no new edit this round; the fix was already on disk when I opened the file, and my work was to re-derive, verify and prove it.

THE FIX ON DISK (src/modules/listings/service.js, uncommitted vs 3136b91)
A new helper at lines 152-154:
  function auditLocalDate(row) { return serializers.publicListing(row).localDate; }
replaces `String(row.local_date)` at the three audit sites, now lines 236 (listing.created), 512 (listing.updated) and 570 (listing.cancelled). This routes the audited date through the exact projection the wire already uses (serializers.isoCalendarDate via publicListing), so the AB-03 trail and the API response can never disagree. src/modules/listings/serializers.js is UNCHANGED — no `isoCalendarDate` export was needed, because publicListing already exposes the value.

CAUSE PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED
Direct pg round-trip of `SELECT '2026-08-17'::date` under four timezones reproduces the verifiers' exact strings and shows the fix is timezone-stable:
  America/Los_Angeles | OLD "Mon Aug 17 2026 00:00:00 GMT-0700 (Pacific Daylight Time)" | NEW "2026-08-17"
  Europe/Paris        | OLD "Mon Aug 17 2026 00:00:00 GMT+0200 (Central European Summer Time)" | NEW "2026-08-17"
  Asia/Tokyo          | OLD "Mon Aug 17 2026 00:00:00 GMT+0900 (Japan Standard Time)" | NEW "2026-08-17"
  UTC                 | OLD "Mon Aug 17 2026 00:00:00 GMT+0000 (Coordinated Universal Time)" | NEW "2026-08-17"
All four row shapes the helper can receive resolve correctly: raw snake_case Date, camelCase repo.toListing Date, `local_date::text` string, and null -> null.

CAVEAT ON COV-05's PROPOSED REMEDY (finding accepted; that one suggested implementation is not)
COV-05 proposes `const asLocalDate = (v) => (v instanceof Date ? mehko.localDateFor(v) : String(v))`. That is incorrect and would ship an off-by-one on every non-LA host. Measured against a stored 2026-08-17:
  Europe/Paris  -> mehko.localDateFor(row.local_date) = 2026-08-16  (shipped isoCalendarDate = 2026-08-17)
  Asia/Tokyo    -> mehko.localDateFor(row.local_date) = 2026-08-16  (shipped isoCalendarDate = 2026-08-17)
Re-projecting a process-local-midnight instant into LA subtracts a day. MTUT-W3-01 warns about exactly this and the shipped code follows MTUT-W3-01's guidance instead. COV-05's alternative suggestion (a pg OID 1082 type parser) was not needed.

FAILURE SCENARIO NO LONGER REPRODUCES
The finding's own reproduce command previously gave "3 failed, 9 passed"; it now gives 12 passed, 12 total — the three block-A assertions (listing.created / listing.updated / listing.cancelled all matching /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ and equal to mehko.localDateFor) pass with NO test edit. Re-run under TZ=Asia/Tokyo: also 12/12. The sibling assertion at tests/mt-ut-quality/mt01-wave3-booking-audit.test.js:168 (`typeof rec.localDate === 'string'`) still passes, as MTUT-W3-01 predicted.

## COV-04 (major) — FIXED: the ADR-010 deny-by-default guards are now exercised directly

**Cause confirmed, not just the symptom.** The finding was reproducible against the current tree: the tracked `coverage/coverage-summary.json` still records `src/modules/listings/access.js` at exactly **84.61% statements / 79.16% branches**, matching the finding verbatim. Root cause is structural, not a missing assertion: every ADR-010 test in the repo (`tests/st-security/st-security-wave3.test.js` ST-06 block, `tests/unit/listings.test.js`, `tests/tc-core/tc02-listing-detail.test.js`, `tests/adr-conformance/*`) drives the gate through session-gated HTTP routes, so the route surface can only ever hand `canViewPreciseLocation` a well-formed authenticated viewer. Both early returns were unreachable from the test surface.

**Fix** — added a `describe('ADR-010 gate: canViewPreciseLocation is deny-by-default when called directly')` block at the end of `/Users/gaetan/Desktop/MSCS/Software Engineer/HomePlate/homeplate/tests/st-security/st-security-wave3.test.js` (no production behaviour changed — the guards were already correct; what was missing was the pin). Four parts:

1. **Viewer table (`test.each`, 7 cases)** — `null`, `undefined`, `{}`, `{userId:'not-a-uuid'}`, `{userId:12345}`, `{userId:"' OR '1'='1"}`, and `{userId:'moderator', roles:['moderator']}` (a claimed moderator role must not buy a way past the identity guard).
2. **listingId table (`test.each`, 7 cases)** — `'not-a-uuid'`, `''`, `"'; DROP TABLE listings; --"`, `null`, `undefined`, `42`, `{}`, all with the *real host* as viewer.
3. **Tripwire client instead of a bare `toBe(false)`** — each case passes a stub for the optional transaction client `access.js` already accepts (`runner(client)` returns `client ?? pool`); it records the SQL and then throws. So a guard that stops short-circuiting fails twice: `expect(client.calls).toEqual([])` reddens *and* the promise rejects instead of resolving `false`. This asserts the stronger property the finding actually cares about — refusal happens **before** any database work, so a non-UUID viewer can never reach the `viewer.userId === hostId` comparison.
4. **Positive control** — host on own listing → `true`; unrelated user → `false`; well-formed but non-existent listing id → `false`. Without this, a bare `return false` pasted at the top of the function would satisfy all 14 deny cases.

**Mutation-verified (3 probes, each applied to `access.js` then reverted from a scratchpad backup):**
- Probe 1 — delete the viewer guard → **7 failed** (all 7 viewer cases; failures read `Received promise rejected instead of resolved: Error: ADR-010 guard fell through to SQL for a malformed caller`).
- Probe 2 — delete the listingId guard → **7 failed** (all 7 listingId cases; the viewer cases stayed green, proving the two tables are independent).
- Probe 3 — `if (true) return false` at the top → **2 failed** (positive control + the moderator/access_log test), the 14 deny cases stayed green. This is exactly the mutation a deny-only table cannot catch, and it is caught.

`access.js` was restored byte-identically after each probe (`git diff` shows only the 3 added doc-comment lines described below).

**Coverage now**: `access.js` is **100% statements / 100% branches / 100% functions / 100% lines** — measured twice, once from `st-security-wave3.test.js` alone and once across all 8 ADR-010-relevant suites.

## COV-08 (minor) — FIXED for the one name in the file I own

Scope note: COV-08 lists nine files; only `src/modules/listings/access.js` is mine this round, so I fixed only its entry, **`PURPOSE_SAFETY_ALERT`**. The other 15 names (`JOB_MODERATION_SCAN`, `EARTH_RADIUS_KM`, `CHANNELS`, `regulation`, `CORRELATION_HEADER`, …) live in files owned by other fixers and I did not touch them.

I re-derived the claim: `grep -rn "PURPOSE_SAFETY_ALERT" src/ tests/ scripts/` returned hits only inside `access.js` itself. Every consumer re-typed the raw literal `'fr07_safety_alert'` (5 places across `tc02-listing-detail`, `unit/listings`, `adr-wave3-invariants`, `verify-adr-wave0-3`, `st-security-wave3`), so a rename of the constant would have been silent. Took the finding's **option (a)** — it is a genuine wave-4 contract, not a pure internal — but made it stronger than a bare literal pin: the new test asserts `PURPOSE_SAFETY_ALERT === 'fr07_safety_alert'` **and** binds it to observed behaviour by calling the moderator branch directly (fresh host/listing/guest/booking/safety_alert/moderator fixtures) and asserting the written `access_log` row's `purpose` equals the exported constant, plus `subject_user_id === host.id` and `resource === 'listing:<id>'` (NFR-13: IDs only, no personal data). Also documented the export in the module's "Public interface" header block — the only change to `access.js` (+3 comment lines, zero behaviour change).

## ADR invariants preserved

No production logic changed. No adapter is called from a request handler (the new tests call a pure decision function directly, not through the worker). The fixtures create their own rows and never truncate, never flush Redis, and never touch another lane's cache identity, per the file's shared-database discipline header.

## Verification runs

- `npx jest tests/st-security/st-security-wave3.test.js` → **46 passed / 46 total** (was 30; +16).
- 8 ADR-010-relevant suites on an isolated lane (`tests/st-security`, `tests/unit/listings.test.js`, `tests/tc-core/tc02-listing-detail.test.js`, `tests/adr-conformance`) → **8 suites / 264 tests, all passed**, `access.js` at 100/100/100/100.
- `npm run lint` (repo-wide `eslint . && prettier --check .`) → **clean**. Prettier reformatted my two `test.each` tables on first pass; re-checked clean afterwards.
- `npm run build` → **clean** (88 files parse, `createApp()` boots against `.env.example`).

## Two caveats the report author should know (not caused by my change)

1. **The default lane is unusable right now.** ~12 concurrent `jest` runs from other fixers are queued on the `homeplate_test_suite` advisory lock (oldest 1h33m). My first `npm test` on the default lane never got the lock in 600 s, and a later default-lane attempt aborted correctly with the env.js guard: *"Redis DB index 1 is already claimed by another Homeplate test run on this host."* I therefore ran full suites on isolated lanes (`homeplate_cov04_test`, `homeplate_cov04b_test`) per the concurrency note.
2. **Both full-suite runs are green except for other fixers' in-flight files.** Each ran **60 suites / 1186 tests** in ~103 s (note: well above the stated 45/943 baseline — other fixers have added suites concurrently). Lane `cov04` → 2 failed: `tests/it-adapters/it01-wave3-worker-paths.test.js` *"IT3-F1 spent dedupe: collapsing onto an already-delivered row secures a FRESH row instead"* (expected `delivered`, received `pending` — this is the IT3-F1 `booking.promote` dedupe finding another fixer owns in `src/modules/bookings/lifecycle.js`) and `tests/tc-booking/tc11-listing-caps.test.js` with a bare `read ECONNRESET` (infrastructure blip under the 12-lane load). Lane `cov04b` → 1 different failure: `tests/adr-conformance/verify-adr-wave0-3.test.js:402` ADR-003 outbox-payload scan flagging `rt02.crash/rt02.retry/rt02.concurrent` job payloads left by `tests/rt-lt-resilience/rt02-wave3-outbox.test.js` (non-string `n` values and non-UUID `entityId`s) — also another fixer's area. **The failing sets are disjoint between the two lanes, and `st-security-wave3.test.js` and everything touching `src/modules/listings/access.js` passed in both.**
3. Both runs printed *"Jest did not exit one second after the test run has completed"* — a pre-existing open-handle issue (a lingering ioredis socket), visible only because I piped output through `tail`. Worth a line in the refreshed verification report; unrelated to this fix.

fixerReports.summary:
Both findings reproduced and fixed at the cause: lane isolation was documented-by-convention and is now derived and self-verifying.

WHAT CHANGED

1. tests/helpers/env.js — a lane owns its resources as a SET.
   - The (guarded) *_test database name is now the lane identity (TEST_DB_NAME). When TEST_REDIS_URL is not given, the Redis DB index is DERIVED from it: `2 + FNV1a32(dbName) % 14` (indices 2..15 — index 0 is the developer's DB, index 1 belongs to the default lane). When OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET is not given it is derived the same way, sanitised to S3/MinIO naming rules (`homeplate-media-<slug>`, hyphenated, <=63 chars). A lane can no longer half-isolate by overriding TEST_DATABASE_URL and silently falling back to the shared Redis index / bucket — the exact half-isolation the CONCURRENCY RULE used to promise away.
   - The default lane (`homeplate_test`) keeps its historical coordinates exactly: redis db 1, bucket homeplate-media-test (asserted; CI is unaffected since it sets no TEST_* overrides).
   - New hard guard: a Redis URL that resolves to DB 0 (explicit `/0` or no index at all) now throws before anything runs — globalSetup FLUSHDBs whatever index it is handed.
   - New `claimLaneResources()`: after the per-database suite lock is held, the lane CLAIMS its Redis index and its bucket with session-scoped `pg_try_advisory_lock` in two distinct lock classes (748301 redis / 748302 bucket) on the shared `postgres` maintenance database — the one lock space every lane on the host shares (globalSetup already connects there to create lane databases, so no new infra/credentials). A claim held by a different lane aborts the run with an actionable message BEFORE any flush; the failed run also drops the database lock it had just taken. If the registry itself is unreachable the run continues with a loud warning (safety net, not a protocol requirement).
   - `acquireSuiteLock()` now takes the database lock FIRST (so two runs of the SAME lane still queue exactly as before) and then the resource claims; `release()` ends both sessions. Exports added: LANE, describeLane, claimLaneResources. tests/rt-lt-resilience/lt01-run.js gets the protection for free — it already goes through acquireSuiteLock().
   - Header CONCURRENCY RULE rewritten to state explicitly that the PostgreSQL advisory lock covers the DATABASE ONLY and says nothing about Redis or object storage, why sharing an index is silently destructive (no eviction, no error), and the one residual gap by construction: lanes split across two PostgreSQL servers that share one Redis host are still unprotected.

2. tests/helpers/globalSetup.js — the FLUSHDB now provably targets state this run owns. The lock handle stashed on globalThis is a small composite whose `end()` releases the database lock AND both resource claims, so the existing globalTeardown call site releases everything without being touched (I only own the files listed in the findings). Added `globalSetup: claimed lane "<db>" (redis db N, bucket B)` printed BEFORE anything destructive, plus the same coordinates in the closing line — a mis-set lane is now visible in the log of the run that would cause the damage, not only in the victim's failures (TCB-W3-07's logging ask).

3. jest.config.js — the parallel-lane comment now says give each lane its own TEST_DATABASE_URL (index and bucket derive from it), that the advisory lock covers neither Redis nor object storage, and that globalSetup claims both and refuses to start on a collision.

ONE PROPOSED REMEDY DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN (the finding itself stands). TCB-W3-07 suggested replacing globalSetup's `redis.flushdb()` with `flushNamespace()` over the `hp:` prefixes. That would not have fixed anything — sessions ARE `hp:session:*`, so a namespace flush destroys a colliding sibling's sessions just as thoroughly — and it would break three ADR-conformance tests (tests/adr-conformance/adr-invariants.test.js:590, adr-wave3-invariants.test.js:948, verify-adr-wave0-3.test.js:915) which assert that EVERY key in the index matches /^hp:(session|ratelimit|cache):/; a partial flush leaves foreign keys behind. Ownership, not key pattern, is what makes the flush safe, so flushdb stays with the reasoning recorded in the comment. For the same reason the claim is a PostgreSQL advisory lock rather than the suggested `SET hp:suite:owner NX EX` marker: a Redis marker key would either fail those keyspace assertions or sit in a namespace that tests/helpers/redis.js flushNamespace() wipes mid-run (silently un-claiming the lane), and a TTL lease needs refreshing from a connection held open in Jest's main process, which stalls Jest's exit. Session-scoped locks give exact liveness with zero keyspace footprint and no stale-lease window.

VERIFICATION (reproduced end to end, on a host that currently has ~10 sibling verifier lanes running)
- Failure scenario no longer reproduces: lane A (`homeplate_rtlt_test`, redis db 14) holding its claims + a live sentinel session key `hp:session:SENTINEL-LIVE-SESSION` in db 14; lane B started with TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/14 aborted in globalSetup with "Redis DB index 14 is already claimed by another Homeplate test run on this host … The 'homeplate_test_suite' PostgreSQL advisory lock is per-database and does NOT cover Redis or object storage. Fix: point this lane at a free index …". `redis-cli -n 14 exists hp:session:SENTINEL-LIVE-SESSION` -> 1 and `dbsize` -> 1 afterwards: the sibling's live session was NOT flushed. Pre-fix, that same command line ran a FLUSHDB.
- Bucket collision aborts too (different db, free index, shared bucket) with the ADR-004/NFR-12 message.
- Half-isolation is gone: a lane setting ONLY TEST_DATABASE_URL now lands on its own derived index 13 and its own bucket and runs green while lane A holds db 14.
- No regression for same-lane runs: a second run on `homeplate_rtlt_test` printed the "waiting for it to finish" warning, queued ~13 s behind the holder, then claimed and passed — it does not abort itself.
- Full suite on an isolated lane: 60 suites / 1186 tests passed in 100.951 s (the tree has grown past the 45/943 baseline while sibling fixers land work). npm run lint clean (eslint + prettier). npm run build clean (4 migrations, 88 files parse, createApp() boots).
- No ADR invariant touched: nothing was added to the request path, no adapter is called inline, no test was weakened or deleted; the change is confined to test bootstrap. The test Redis keyspace gains no new keys, so the ADR-conformance namespace scans still pass (they are in the 60 green suites).

OBSERVATION FOR THE PARENT (pre-existing, outside my files, worth a finding of its own): `npm test` prints "Jest did not exit one second after the test run has completed" and the main process then hangs forever holding ONE lingering Redis socket. Because jest runs in-band at maxWorkers=1, a test suite that never closes its Redis client keeps the runner alive. I confirmed by lsof on five hung runners (elapsed 2 min to 1 h 52 min, i.e. started well before my edits): each holds exactly one ESTABLISHED socket to 127.0.0.1:6379 and ZERO PostgreSQL connections — so my lock/registry clients are released correctly by teardown, but a hung runner keeps holding the suite advisory lock, which is why several sibling lanes have been sitting at 0% CPU for over an hour. Recommend hunting the missing closeTestRedis()/closeRedis() (or adding --detectOpenHandles to one run) as a separate item; it is the reason concurrent verification on this box appears to stall.

MECHANISM REPRODUCED. src/adapters/maps.js writes two value shapes under the audited hp:cache:maps:* glob: geocode caches the bare {lat,lng,areaLabel} (cachedLookup line 298 writes publicValue from liveGeocode/mockGeocode) and searchArea caches the envelope {areas:[…]} (lines 362/381). globalSetup flushes Redis once per RUN and maxWorkers=1 shares one Redis DB across suites, so any earlier suite that leaves a search envelope behind turned the audit red.

- Deterministic probe (isolated Redis DB …/9, /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/cov02-repro.js): after one searchArea + one geocode the namespace holds BOTH shapes ("areaLabel,lat,lng | areas"); a verbatim copy of the pre-fix assertion threw on 2 of 4 keys; the flattening version passed over 8 coordinate-bearing objects.
- Jest-level NEGATIVE CONTROL: I restored the committed (3136b91) file and forced suite order with a scratch sequencer. tests/unit/search.test.js is the actual leaver (it ends with 4 hp:cache:maps:search:* pairs still in Redis; tests/unit/adapter-maps.test.js and tests/tc-core/tc01-search.test.js each flush the cache namespace in beforeEach, which is why the naive orderings pass). Running search.test.js then the PRE-FIX adr suite reproduced the exact reported error at line 273: `Expected Array ["areaLabel","lat","lng"] Received Array ["areas"]`. The fixed file was restored immediately after.

FIX (cause, not symptom — the assertion was strengthened, never weakened). The audit loop is now shape-aware: each cached value is flattened into its coordinate-bearing objects (`if (Array.isArray(entry.areas)) items.push(...entry.areas); else items.push(entry);`) before the unchanged ['areaLabel','lat','lng'] key check, the coarsen-is-a-no-op check and the street-label regex run over every element. That removes the order dependence AND closes the audit hole the finding identified: searchArea's cached coordinates — exactly where location SEARCH results live — are now audited for ADR-010 public precision instead of being skipped. I additionally added `expect(Object.keys(entry).sort()).toEqual(['areas'])` on the envelope itself, so a sibling field smuggled alongside `areas` cannot ride into Redis unaudited; maps.js writes publicValue verbatim, so this holds today and fails loudly if the envelope ever grows a precise-coordinate field.

VERIFICATION. POSITIVE CONTROL in the failing order (search.test.js first, then adr-invariants): 4 suites / 93 tests passed. FULL tests/ tree in a dedicated isolated lane (TEST_DATABASE_URL=homeplate_cov02b_test, TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/13, OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET=homeplate-media-cov02b) — the same configuration in which the verifier saw it fail: **60 suites / 1186 tests, 0 failures, 100.9 s** (includes the untracked wave-4 verifier suites; adr-invariants.test.js, adr-wave3-invariants.test.js and verify-adr-wave0-3.test.js all PASS). `npm run lint` (eslint + prettier) exits 0. Lane database and Redis indices 9/12/13 were dropped/flushed afterwards.

NOTES FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR. (1) The working tree already carried a first-pass version of this flattening when I started — I re-derived the finding from scratch, proved it against commit 3136b91, kept the fix and hardened it. (2) The same file's git diff contains one hunk I did NOT author and did not touch: the ADR-001/003 transport-importer list now expects outbox/handlers/safetyAlert.js (a wave-4 addition). It was present before my first edit and is correct — it is what makes the pre-fix negative-control runs show a second, unrelated failure. (3) Environment note: at the time of this run 19 sibling jest processes were live, several stuck 1-2 h on the shared-lane advisory lock; two of my own runs were also pipe-buffered through `tail` and produced no visible progress. I killed only my own two and re-ran with a real log file in an isolated lane. Anyone verifying this repo concurrently should use per-lane TEST_DATABASE_URL/TEST_REDIS_URL/OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET rather than queueing on the shared lock. (4) No ADR invariant was relaxed: no adapter moved onto a request path, nothing was published unmoderated, and only public-precision values are asserted to be cacheable."

COV-03 (IT3-F1 safety net unverified) — confirmed exactly as reported: on the pre-fix tree `lifecycle.isLivePendingJob` had 0 function hits, because the only IT3-F1 test drives the "deduped onto the row I am delivering" leg, which returns at the `job.id === deliveringJobId` check one line earlier. No source change was needed — the four legs of the decision table all behave correctly — so the fix is the missing coverage. Added 4 worker-path tests to tests/it-adapters/it01-wave3-worker-paths.test.js (plus a `promoteRows(bookingId)` helper and a decision-table comment):
  1. LIVE-DEDUPE — a second promote row (disambiguated key) is delivered early through the REAL worker while the base-key row is still live; asserts the outcome is a reschedule onto the pre-existing row, exactly 2 promote rows remain and the surviving pending row IS the base row (drives isLivePendingJob → true).
  2. SPENT-DEDUPE — the base-key row is marked delivered first; asserts a fresh row keyed `<baseKey>:r<jobId>` is created at the listing's true start (drives isLivePendingJob → false).
  3. CLAIM-LOCKED — a concurrent transaction holds `FOR UPDATE` on the base row (what worker.js CLAIM_SQL does for the duration of a handler); asserts the locked row is NOT trusted and a fresh disambiguated row is secured. This pins the `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` rationale the doc comment claims.
  4. FAIL-CLOSED — both candidate dedupe keys are occupied by non-live rows; asserts the handler throws (BOOKING_PROMOTE_UNSECURED), the worker leaves the delivered row `pending` with attempt_count 1, `last_error` matching "no replacement row could be secured", a backed-off available_at and the booking still `pending`.
Each test fails under the obvious mutations (predicate stuck true, stuck false, throw removed). Coverage after: isLivePendingJob 5 hits, securePromotionSchedule 6, and the previously-dead `if (!secured)` throw block is now executed; no statement in the IT3-F1 machinery is uncovered.

fixerReports.summary:
STS-W3-01 CONFIRMED and FIXED at the cause, in src/modules/users/repo.js only.

Cause: serializeUser() called fieldCrypto.decrypt() unconditionally on phone_enc and the three emergency_contact_*_enc columns. decrypt() throws by contract on anything that is not a canonical, current-key ciphertext, so ONE bad column made the owner's own profile a permanent 500 on both GET and PATCH /api/users/me — with no way for the account to repair the value, and a FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY rotation would do it to every user at once.

Fix (src/modules/users/repo.js): new private helper decryptForOwner(row, column) wraps decrypt() in try/catch, returns null on failure and emits exactly one logger.warn per column with IDs only — { module:'usersRepo', userId, column, err } / 'undecryptable PII column — rendering null'. serializeUser now reads all four *_enc columns through it. fieldCrypto.decrypt itself is UNCHANGED (still throws — silent corruption stays impossible, NFR-13); the helper is not exported (no new public surface, no dead export). Header traceability updated with the NFR-08 line. This matches the precedent already in src/outbox/handlers/safetyAlert.js:152, which has caught the same failure since wave 4 groundwork.

Reproduction, before and after (standalone probe, lane-isolated, holding the suite advisory lock per tests/helpers/env.js option (a)):
- pre-fix path proven still throwing: decrypt('enc:v1:fixture') -> RangeError: fieldCrypto.decrypt: ciphertext too short — truncated or corrupted (this is the exception that used to propagate out of serializeUser -> 500).
- post-fix, four states, each with GET then PATCH {fullName:'Plain Name'}:
  * phone_enc='enc:v1:fixture'                    -> 200 / 200, phone=null
  * phone_enc encrypted under a DIFFERENT 32-byte key (real GCM auth failure = key rotation) -> 200 / 200, phone=null
  * all three emergency_contact_*_enc non-canonical -> 200 / 200, emergencyContact={name:null,phone:null,email:null}, phone still decrypts correctly
  * CONTROL healthy row                            -> 200 / 200, phone='+14155550142'
  No response leaked ciphertext ('enc:v1:'), a stack, or an internal message in any case — the ST-06/NFR-13 property the verifier asserted survives. The WARN lines carry only module/userId/column/error type+message; no ciphertext and no plaintext (checked by regex over the captured lines).

rejected.id: TCC-05 (root-cause attribution only — the finding itself is valid and is fixed)
rejected.why: The finding blames src/lib/cache.set swallowing Redis errors ('a failed cache write costs latency, never correctness'). That is a real property but it is NOT what produced the observed 'Expected: > 0, Received: 0'. The actual defect was in the assertion itself: tests/tc-core/tc01-search.test.js:214 used a SINGLE-PASS `redis.scan('0','MATCH','hp:cache:search:page:*','COUNT',500)` as an existence check. Redis only guarantees a complete iteration when the cursor returns to '0'; COUNT is a per-call bucket hint, and MATCH filters AFTER the bucket slice is chosen. Deterministic reproduction (scratchpad script, redis DB index 9, key written with EX 60): ambient keys=400 -> cursor=0 matched=1; 600 -> cursor=395 matched=0; 1000 -> cursor=446 matched=0; 2000 -> cursor=1148 matched=0; 3000 -> cursor=468 matched=0 — while in every case the full cursor loop matched=1 and a direct EXISTS returned 1 with ttl=60. So above ~512 keys in the index the old assertion reports a FALSE NEGATIVE for a key that provably exists. That threshold is reached in normal operation, not only under 4-way contention: after a full-suite run on an isolated lane the index held 570 keys (session/ratelimit keys accumulate all run and flushNamespace('cache') does not clear them). Note also that a genuinely dropped cache.set could not have produced only this failure — the very next assertion in the same test (repeat query performs ZERO maps.searchArea calls) would have failed too, and it did not. Consequently I did NOT modify src/lib/cache.js: swallowing write failures is the binding NFR-09 degraded-mode invariant and changing it would be a regression, not a fix.

fixerReports.summary:
TCC-05 fixed in tests/tc-core/tc01-search.test.js only; src/lib/cache.js is deliberately untouched.

CAUSE. The flaky line was not a dropped cache write — it was an invalid existence check. `SCAN 0 MATCH hp:cache:search:page:* COUNT 500` samples part of the keyspace; once the shared test index holds more than ~512 keys it returns a non-zero cursor and zero matches for a key that exists. Reproduced deterministically (see rejected/attribution note): at 600, 1000, 2000 and 3000 ambient keys the single pass matched 0 while a full cursor loop matched 1 and a direct EXISTS returned 1 with ttl=60. The sibling ADR-010 test in the same file, which already looped the cursor to completion, never failed — exactly the asymmetry the verifier observed. A full-suite run leaves 570 keys in the lane's index, so the old assertion was a coin flip in ordinary runs, not only under 4-way contention.

FIX (strengthens, does not weaken). Added `pageCacheKey(query)`, which derives the EXACT Redis key through the production path — `src/schemas/search.js` boundary parse -> `searchService.normalizeQuery` -> `searchService.cacheKeyFor` — and `readCachedPage(query)`, which reads that key with GET+TTL. The cache test now asserts more than before: the key matches /^hp:cache:search:page:[0-9a-f]{32}$/ (digest-keyed namespace, ADR-010/AB-08 — no location text in a key name), the value is present, TTL is > 0 AND <= config.search.cacheTtlSeconds, and the cached payload is THIS query's page (results === [inWindowA.id]) rather than merely 'some page key exists'. The zero-adapter-call spy assertion is unchanged. `readCachedPage` also re-issues the identical query for up to 2 s if no page is there — that covers the finding's cache.set-swallow scenario without softening anything: if a page is never cached, the assertions still fail. The ADR-010 cache-audit test now reads the page under audit by exact key and includes that value in the swept blob, so the ADR-010 leak audit can no longer be satisfied by an accidentally empty sweep; the full-cursor sweep over hp:cache:* and its key-name assertions are unchanged.

VERIFICATION. The failure scenario no longer reproduces: the file passes on the default lane (14/14), and passes again on an isolated lane while a background process kept ~6000 ambient hp:session:* keys in that Redis index — the exact condition under which the old single-pass SCAN returns 0. Full suite on an isolated lane: 60 suites / 1186 tests passed in 106 s (the tree has grown past the 45/943 baseline because other fixers are landing tests concurrently). `npm run lint` clean repo-wide. No ADR invariant touched: no adapter is called inline from a request handler, the ADR-005 read-path exception is untouched, cache.set still swallows failures per NFR-09.

NOTE FOR THE REPORT AUTHOR (I did not edit docs/verification-report.md — not in my finding's file list, and it is owned by the reporting phase). Suggested wording: 'Parallel jest lanes must each set TEST_DATABASE_URL, TEST_REDIS_URL and OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET; sharing an index only queues behind the suite advisory lock and lets another run flush a live cache cell. Latency measurements and any assertion about cache-key existence are authoritative only on an otherwise idle machine — and cache-existence assertions must read an exact key, never a single-pass SCAN.' Also worth carrying forward: the still-open verifier reports of tests/unit/adapter-maps.test.js:489, tests/tc-booking/tc13-notifications.test.js and tests/unit/hosts-media.test.js failing in the same contended run — adapter-maps.test.js is the one other suite that scans the cache namespace and should be checked for the same single-pass-SCAN pattern (it is outside my file scope, so I did not touch it).

fixerReports.summary:
TCC-02 reproduced and fixed on the FR-01 search surface (the file I own). The FR-02 detail / direct-id-booking half is deliberately NOT changed - see the residual note below; it needs a decision in files I do not own.

WHAT WAS WRONG
src/modules/search/repo.js VISIBLE_PREDICATES carried only the FR-08/AB-01 publication invariant (approved + active + future). It had no NFR-12 erasure direction, so a soft-deleted host's listings stayed in the public index while GET /api/hosts/:id already 404'd (hosts/repo.findHost filters users.deleted_at).

FIX (one predicate, plus the reasoning in comments)
VISIBLE_PREDICATES gained a fourth fixed fragment, shared by buildSearchQuery and buildCountQuery:
  `(SELECT u.deleted_at IS NULL FROM users u WHERE u.id = listings.host_id)`
Still fixed SQL text with zero caller data (NFR-11/ST-04 unchanged), still coarse-coordinates-only (ADR-010 untouched), no adapter call, no new read path.

WHY A SCALAR SUBQUERY AND NOT `EXISTS` (this matters - the obvious form regresses an acceptance gate)
I first wrote the finding's proposed `AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM users u WHERE u.id = l.host_id AND u.deleted_at IS NULL)`. It passes every functional test but FAILS LT-02: PostgreSQL pulls an EXISTS sublink up into a semi-join, and on the freshly bulk-loaded listings table LT-02 measures (globalSetup resets the schema, the volume seed batch-inserts, autovacuum has not ANALYZEd yet) the planner picks a HASH semi join and abandons listings_scheduled_start_idx. Reproduced deterministically:
  npx jest tests/rt-lt-resilience/lt01-lt02-wave3.test.js -t "EXPLAIN ANALYZE"  ->
  'LT-02: unjustified sequential scan on listings for shape "bare" (page query; matchFraction=1.00)'
An expression sublink is never pulled up, so the scalar form stays a per-row users_pkey lookup applied as a filter; the LIMIT-20 page evaluates it ~20 times and the plan cannot flip with the statistics. Same test with the scalar form: PASS, all twelve shapes index-driven - {"bare.page":0.339,"bare.count":0.745,"cuisine.page":0.188,"cuisine.count":0.21,"host.page":0.034,"host.count":0.038,"window.page":0.313,"window.count":0.802,"geo.page":0.4,"geo.count":0.841,"combined.page":0.208,"combined.count":0.255} ms. (It also removed the pre-existing justified seq scan on the bare COUNT query.) The comment block above VISIBLE_PREDICATES records this so nobody "simplifies" it back. Fail-closed bonus: a missing users row would yield NULL, i.e. hidden.

FAILURE SCENARIO NO LONGER REPRODUCES
Probe (scratchpad/probe-tcc02.js, holding the suite advisory lock per tests/helpers/env; seeds host + host_profile + approved/active/future listing with cuisine probecuisine<RUN>, then UPDATE users SET deleted_at = now()):
  PROBE[live host]    search status 200 n= 1
  PROBE[deleted host] search status 200 n= 0  ids=[]
  PROBE[sql] pre-fix predicate matches 1 row(s); current buildCountQuery matches 0 row(s)   <- the row is still there; the predicate is what hides it
  PROBE[host page]    GET /api/hosts/:id status 404
  PROBE[detail]       GET /api/listings/:id status 200   <- residual, see below

VERIFICATION
- npm test on an isolated lane (TEST_DATABASE_URL=...homeplate_fixsearch_test, TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/12, OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET=homeplate-media-fixsearch): Test Suites 60 passed / 60, Tests 1186 passed / 1186, 104.662 s. Includes LT-01 (200 VUs, 45 s: errorRate 0, overall p95 154.6 ms, search p95 4.1 ms - measured while ~6 other agents' suites were hammering the same host, so it is a pessimistic number), LT-02, ST-04 security lane, adr-conformance lanes.

TCC-03 resolved by option (b) — the FR-01 acceptance sentence was corrected and the decision recorded; src/modules/search/service.js keeps its behaviour (only its documentation was sharpened). Evidence that option (a) is not implementable: the same FR-01 criterion requires that "a second identical query performs zero adapter calls (assert on the adapter spy)" (the NFR-01 hot-path guarantee behind the 500 ms p95 budget). A request that makes zero adapter calls cannot observe that the provider is failing — in the reproduced probe (warm the page cache, then force maps.searchArea to reject, repeat the identical query) nothing in the system ever fails, so there is no signal to flag. Satisfying the old sentence literally requires probing Maps on every cache hit, which deletes the sentence immediately preceding it and burns free-tier quota (SRS §2.4). The SRS does not ask for the flag either: NFR-09 and SRS §2.1.6 require degraded mode to "display an appropriate error message, use cache or previously stored data where available, and defer non-critical actions" — nothing labels a fresh cache hit, and per SPMP §1.1.2 the SRS baseline outranks this derived inventory. A page-cache hit is also not degraded data: it was built from PostgreSQL under a healthy geocode and lives at most SEARCH_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (default 60 s, src/config/schema.js:157).

fixerReports.summary:
MTUT-W3-03 fixed in /Users/gaetan/Desktop/MSCS/Software Engineer/HomePlate/homeplate/package.json (the only file I touched).

REPRODUCED FIRST, exactly as reported. `npm run test:a11y` printed "Running axe-core 4.13.0 in chrome-headless" then "Error: session not created: This version of ChromeDriver only supports Chrome version 152 / Current browser version is 151.0.7922.138 …" and exited 2. All three compounding causes confirmed independently: (1) `npx --yes @axe-core/cli` resolves the tool and its ChromeDriver at run time, unpinned, so the run is not reproducible and not CI-able; (2) it targeted one URL while NFR-07's acceptance in requirements-inventory.json enumerates seven interfaces; (3) `curl -m 5 http://localhost:5173` → HTTP 000 / exit 7 and `client/` does not exist, so the script has never had a subject.

FIX (cause, not symptom). The cause is that package.json advertised an accessibility capability with no subject, no harness and no pinned toolchain, and failed with a message that blamed the developer's browser — which reads as "a real audit that is merely misconfigured". `test:a11y` no longer shells out to `npx --yes`; it is now a state-aware guard that exits 1 with an accurate explanation. It checks `fs.existsSync('client')`: with no client/ it says the responsive React client ships in waves 5-6 (SRS 2.1.2) so there is nothing to audit, and points at build-plan unit U7-A11Y-UX; once client/ lands it instead spells out the wave-5 wiring required (pin @axe-core/playwright plus a browser package as devDependencies — never `npx --yes` — and add a tests/mt-ut-quality/ spec that boots the Vite preview server and audits all seven NFR-07 interfaces at wcag2a/wcag2aa with zero serious/critical violations plus keyboard-traversal checks, then replace the script). Both paths restate that the 5-participant moderated study (SRS §4.5) is a recorded human activity. It needs no network and no browser, so its result is now deterministic on any machine. I verified both branches (the client-present branch by running the same expression in a scratchpad directory containing a client/ dir).

Why I did NOT add the axe/browser devDependencies now: package-lock.json is outside my file scope and is not in this finding. Adding devDependencies to package.json without regenerating the lockfile makes `npm ci` fail with EUSAGE (lock out of sync), which would break every install and CI job. Vendoring the pinned browser toolchain belongs with the wave-5 spec that uses it, in one `npm install` that updates both files.

VERIFICATION. `npm run test:a11y` → the wave-5 message, exit 1, no ChromeDriver error, no network access (failure scenario no longer reproduces). `npm run lint` → eslint clean, "All matched files use Prettier code style!", exit 0 (re-run after a concurrent fixer's scan:zap scripts landed in the same file — their edit and mine coexist; I did not revert it). `npm run build` → 4 migrations valid, 88 files parse, createApp() boots against .env.example, exit 0. Evidence of the real cause: `git status --porcelain` shows verify-adr-wave0-3.test.js as UNTRACKED (`??`) — a brand-new file from a concurrent fixer this round — and it scans the ENTIRE outbox_jobs table, so it picks up the synthetic numeric payloads `{ n: i }` enqueued by tests/rt-lt-resilience/rt02-outbox.test.js:263,272, which is committed at c4f33b3 (waves 0-2) and unmodified in the working tree. STS-W3-04 confirmed and fixed. I reproduced it first: `which zap-baseline.py zap.sh` -> both not found, `docker image ls | grep -i zap` -> empty, no scan script in package.json, no ZAP step in .github/. AB-06's last acceptance clause genuinely had no owner.

WHAT I ADDED (only the two files the finding assigns me):

1. package.json - three scripts. `scan:zap` = `scan:zap:run` (the scan) then `scan:zap:report` (the gate), and the gate decides the exit status.
   - `scan:zap:run` runs `zap-baseline.py` from `ghcr.io/zaproxy/zaproxy:stable` with `docs/results/` mounted as `/zap/wrk`, emitting zap-baseline.html/.md/.json. Overridable via ZAP_TARGET_URL, ZAP_SPIDER_MINUTES, ZAP_REPORT_JSON.
   - `scan:zap:report` parses the JSON report, prints the alert table by risk level and EXITS 1 IF ANY ALERT IS HIGH (riskcode>=3), naming the alert and the first URLs. A missing report is also exit 1, so a scan that never reached the app can never be read as a pass. This turns "reports no high-risk alerts" from an eyeballed clause into a measured one.
2. .github/workflows/zap-baseline.yml - "ZAP baseline (AB-06)", `workflow_dispatch` only (opt-in, not a new push-CI dependency, per the proposed fix). rejected.id: W3-ADR-05 (the proposed fix's literal wording — rejected; the finding itself is accepted and fixed)
rejected.why: The proposed fix asks ADR-009 to state 'Weeks are Monday-anchored ... (a rolling 7-day window is the stricter alternative; deferred)' and to 'record the team's ratification date'. I did not do that, for three reasons and I implemented a neutral fix instead. (1) The run brief for this wave says the weekly-window question (TCB-01 / ADRC-W3-03) is a SPEC AMBIGUITY to 'report it, do not silently pick'; writing the Monday anchor into the Decision table is picking it, by agent fiat, in the one document that is binding. (2) There is no ratification date to record — build-plan open question 1 schedules the decision for CDR and it has not happened; the same rule the plan applies to the ADR-008 human label sign-off ('No agent may record it') applies here, so recording a date would fabricate a team decision record. (3) The reading being proposed for ratification is the materially weaker one: ADR-009 Consequences and tests/tc-booking/tcb-w3-reverify.test.js reproduce 120 meals — twice the 60/week cap — inside a single 7-day span (30-seat listings on Sat 2031-03-08, Sun 03-09, Mon 03-10, Tue 03-11 all return 201). Blessing that by default is a substantive safety decision, not a documentation tidy-up. The finding's *substance* (a reader of ADR-009 alone could implement the rolling window and contradict the tests) is real and is now closed without choosing a reading.

The finding was derived against commit 3136b91, not the working tree. Verified with `git show '3136b91:ADRs/# ADR-009 MEHKO capacity limits.md'`: at that commit the ADR did indeed name only the number and the timezone. In the current (uncommitted) working tree it already carried a full 'Weekly window shape — OPEN, not ratified' section, a Status line flagging the open sub-decision, an Amendment log entry, and a Consequences bullet quantifying the evasion — added by an earlier round of this run. Likewise the finding's claim that requirements-inventory.json FR-11 'says Monday-anchored ... NOT a rolling 7-day window' is true of 3136b91 only; the working-tree inventory now carries a specAmbiguity block (findingId TCB-W3-05) and marks the weekly clause PROVISIONAL, so I left it untouched. Only the residual gap the finding names last was genuinely still open and that is what I fixed.

fixerReports.summary:

REPRODUCTION: grep -nE '(SELECT|INSERT INTO|UPDATE |DELETE FROM)' src/modules/media/routes.js returns 4 hits; lines 29, 30 and 79 are the transitional comments and line 81 is the single executable statement:
  const { rows } = await query(`SELECT author_id FROM reviews WHERE id = $1`, [entityId]);
Exactly as the verifier described.

WHY I DID NOT FIX IT (four independent blockers):
1. The proposed fix requires creating src/modules/reviews/repo.js. tests/coverage/coverage-lane.test.js:66-73 is an ACTIVE, PASSING scope guard that asserts fs.existsSync(src/modules/<mod>) === false for reviews/messaging/moderation/privacy. Creating that directory turns a green test red, and the only way to make it pass again is to edit the guard - weakening a test, which the rules forbid. The guard is legitimate: 'safety' was removed from that list only when U4-SAFETY actually landed.
2. The authoritative plan already owns and schedules it. docs/_generated/build-plan.md SS6.4 states verbatim: 'Carried, not a defect - the review-authorship SELECT in src/modules/media/routes.js. One parameterized statement lives in the routes file because the reviews module does not exist yet; the header documents it and U4-REVIEWS owns its removal. Listed so it is not re-discovered.' build-plan line 141 lists src/modules/media/routes.js (authorship SELECT -> reviews repo) as a U4-REVIEWS deliverable. The finding's own Proposed fix agrees: 'No action is needed before wave 4.'
3. Every alternative placement is an unlisted file AND a worse layering. src/modules/hosts/repo.js already queries the reviews table (getReviewStats :116, listApprovedReviews :137) but owns 'reviews ABOUT a host', not review-by-id authorship; src/modules/media/repo.js owns media_objects. Putting a reviews query in either makes a repo own a table it does not own - a lateral move wave 4 must undo.
4. Wave 4 is landing in this tree RIGHT NOW (src/modules/safety/, src/schemas/safety.js, src/outbox/handlers/safetyAlert.js untracked; my jest run printed 'globalSetup: test database is locked by another suite run'). Creating src/modules/reviews/ would collide head-on with the concurrent U4-REVIEWS implementer.

NO INTERIM RISK: the statement is parameterized (NFR-11 intact, no injection). entityId is zod-validated as uuid.optional() at src/schemas/media.js:69, so a hostile entityId is a 422 at the boundary and can never reach pg as a 22P02 -> 500 (AB-06/ST-04 holds). All ADR invariants preserved: no adapter is reachable from this request path (tests/unit/hosts-media.test.js asserts src/modules/media/routes.js contains no require of src/adapters/, and the /uploads handler opens no socket to the storage endpoint).
